generated_text: I can't believe it's already been a week since the baby was born. Time just flies when you're busy with all the baby stuff, don’t you think? Oh, I know, I feel the same. So, do you remember that time we tried to hitchhike from Lyon to Nice? I still can’t believe we got picked up by a guy who was clearly more interested in his dog than in driving. Oh, don’t even start. I think that dog was more of a distraction than anything else. I mean, he was a golden retriever, and he was basically sitting in the passenger seat the whole time, staring at us like we were the most interesting thing in the world. Yeah, and then he just started asking us about our travel plans, like we were some sort of expert on Europe. I think he thought we were backpackers with no idea what we were doing. Exactly! And I was trying to explain that I was doing a PhD on the cultural impact of tourism in the EU, and he just laughed and said, “Oh, you’ve got it all figured out, then.” It was so frustrating. I was trying to be professional, but he didn’t even take the hint. I think he just wanted to talk about his vacations in the Caribbean. I mean, we did end up getting to Nice in the end, didn’t we? And it was a pretty scenic drive. I was just thinking about that the other day when I was in the pub, and I started wondering how long the EU will keep its borders open like that. I know, right? It’s been so long since we’ve had to worry about visas or anything. I can’t imagine traveling without being able to move freely across the continent. It feels like a privilege. Definitely. I was in Prague last year and I had this amazing time. Just wandered around the Old Town, got lost in the Latin Quarter, and ended up at this little café that served the best coffee I’ve ever had. You always do that, don’t you? Just wander around until you find something incredible. You’re like a walking tourist guide. Well, I do have a PhD in tourism, you know. I think it’s part of the job. I guess so. Anyway, I’m just trying to get back to the point that the EU is one of the best things that ever happened to travel. I mean, think about how many places you can go without even leaving the continent.

I just made a new dessert recipe last night — it’s a twist on a classic. It’s like a panna cotta, but with some local berries from the market. I think it’s going to be a hit. Oh, you made  panna cotta ? That sounds fancy! I thought that was something you only saw on the TV show  Nailed It . I’ve never had panna cotta. Is it like a custard? You can’t really tell it’s not custard. I think it’s going to be perfect with some fresh fruit on top. Do you think we can make it again? I really want to try it. Maybe we can have a dessert night? Maybe I need to invest in more properties — or maybe I should just focus on the desserts. I think I’d rather have a sweet than a monopoly. I agree! The desserts are way more fun. I’d rather eat a slice of cake than play Monopoly for an hour.

I can't believe we've been stuck in this traffic for over an hour. It's like the whole city's decided to take a break today. Yeah, I know, it's ridiculous. I was just thinking about how we're supposed to be on our way to the meeting in two hours. This isn't going to help anyone. I know, I know. It’s just so frustrating. Yeah, that’s a good idea. And maybe while we’re there, we can actually talk about what we’re going to say in the meeting. I’ve been trying to get my thoughts together, but I’m still not sure. I’m with you. I’ve been working on my notes all morning, but I still feel like I’m not ready.

I've been thinking a lot lately, you know. I mean, I've had a few years off now, and I still feel like I'm waiting for something to happen. Not like I've got nothing to do, but it's just... quiet. You ever feel like that? I know exactly what you mean. I've been in the same position for over ten years. It's like the world moves on without you, and you're just stuck in this waiting room. You know, I was a bit of a doer when I was younger. But now... well, it's just different. It's a tough spot to be in, isn’t it? I’ve always been more on the quiet side, but even I have days where I feel like I’m not contributing anything. I was a childminder, so I used to be busy all the time. Now, I’ve got the house to myself, and it’s... peaceful in a way, but also lonely at times. Yeah, you can’t deny the loneliness. I’ve got my mates, but they’re all over the place. Some of them are still working, and some have moved away. I feel like I’m not part of anything anymore. It’s not the same as when I was working. I know. I often think about the days when I had a routine. I had a job, I had a schedule, and I knew what I was doing each day. Now, it’s all just... spontaneous. Spontaneous in a bad way. You don’t know what’s coming next. I think it's the way we’ve been raised, too. We were taught to work, to have a purpose. But now, with everything that's happened, it's hard to find that same drive. I often wonder if I’d be better off staying in the job I left. But then again, I don’t know if I’d even have the energy. That’s the thing, isn’t it? We’re used to being busy, but when you’re not, it’s hard to figure out what to do with yourself. I've tried taking up new hobbies, but honestly, I just don’t have the energy for anything these days. Yeah, I tried gardening. It wasn’t bad, but it was just too much work. I mean, I had a garden, but I couldn’t keep it up.

I can’t believe we've been working on Honest Skincare for three months now and still haven’t launched. I keep telling myself it’ll be ready by the end of the year, but then I get distracted by other things. I know, I’ve been trying to help with the branding, but it’s harder than I thought. I mean, you want it to be authentic and trustworthy, but how do you balance that with making it stand out in the market? Exactly. It’s a tough spot to be in. I was thinking the other day that maybe we need to test our product with a small group of people before we go full steam ahead. I heard about this thing called "pre-orders" where you let people reserve a product before it’s available. It’s a way to gauge interest and get some early feedback. That’s a good idea. It could also help us with our marketing. If we can show that people are interested in our product early on, it might help us get more visibility. I mean, if we can get a few reviews or testimonials from early users, that could really boost our credibility. I like that. But I’m worried about the logistics. How do we manage shipping and returns if we start selling online? I remember when I started my small business selling handmade candles, I had to deal with a lot of issues with packaging and customer service. I know, it’s a big commitment. But maybe you can use social media to your advantage. You could start a page on Instagram or Facebook to share your process, your story, and your product. People love authenticity, especially in the beauty industry. That’s true. I’ve been thinking about doing just that. Maybe I can show the journey of the product, from sourcing the ingredients to the final packaging. It could be a way to build a connection with our customers. That sounds amazing. I could help you with the content if you want. I have some experience with digital marketing and content creation. We could even do a little campaign for your holiday plans. We’re going to Spain next month, right? Yeah, we’re thinking of going to the coast. It’s a way for us to reset and get inspired. I think a short break might help us get back on track with Honest Skincare.

I just got a call from the council, love. They said they’re planning to redevelop the old library building in the town center. I don’t know if that’s a good thing or not. It’s a bit of a shame, honestly. That place has been around since the 1950s. I remember going there as a kid with my mum, and she used to tell me all sorts of stories about the old books and the librarian who used to wear a bowtie. Oh, that’s a real shame. I was just reading an article the other day about how many public spaces are being redeveloped without enough thought given to preserving history. I think it’s a pity when places like that get torn down. It’s not just about the building—it’s about the memories and the community. Exactly, and I’ve been thinking about how much the library meant to so many people. It was a second home for a lot of us. Even after I left teaching, I’d go there to read and just sit in the quiet. I even used to bring my students there when I was still teaching, just to give them a taste of what it was like to be in a real library. That sounds lovely. I’ve always believed that libraries are important, especially for people who don’t have access to books at home. I mean, I was lucky enough to go to a good school, but not everyone has that privilege. If the council is planning to replace it, I hope they at least consider keeping some of the original elements. I hope so too. I’m not sure what the future holds, but I’d hate to see it disappear completely. I was just talking to my sister about how we used to walk there together every Saturday. Do you remember? You used to read a book every week and then come home telling me all about the characters. It was one of those little things that made life feel special. Oh, yes, I remember. I used to read those books aloud to you when we were kids. It was a little ritual, really. I think we both missed that a bit. It’s funny how those small things can stick with you. Absolutely. I think we should write to the council and let them know what we think.

I can't believe it's already December. I feel like we just had the first snowfall, and now we're already on the verge of Christmas. I’m so ready for the holidays, but I also feel a little anxious about the whole process. Yeah, I know what you mean. I’m trying to keep my head down with the heating bill, but I reckon it’s going to be another record cold winter. I’ve already got the thermostat set to 18°C, but I’m not sure if that’s enough. My kids are already asking for warm socks and hot chocolate. Oh, I’ve been trying to make my own mulberry jam this year. It’s not exactly easy, but I think it’s worth it. I remember my grandmother used to make this every Christmas, and I wanted to keep the tradition alive. I think it turned out decent—maybe even better than last year. Mulberry jam? I haven’t even thought about that. I was just planting some mulberry trees in my garden last week. I figured they’d take a few years to bear fruit, but maybe I can use them for something else. I’m also thinking about starting to make my own tools for the workshop. I’ve got a few old ones, but I’m curious if there are any new gadgets that could help with my craft. That’s a great idea. I’ve been telling my colleagues at work about my new projects, and one of them mentioned a tool he uses for precision work. I think it’s called a CNC machine. I’m not sure how it works, but it sounds like it could be useful. I wonder if it’s something you could use in your shop, Sam? I’m not sure about the machine, but the tools themselves are always useful. I’ve been trying to maintain my old equipment, but I’m getting a bit tired of fixing things. My sister retired last year, and she told me about how she used to work in manufacturing. She said it was a lot of work, but she enjoyed the challenge. That’s interesting. I’m actually considering taking a break from my PhD next year. I’ve been working on my research for so long, and I think it’s time to take a step back.

I can’t believe we’re still using these old cutlery sets. I thought Mum promised she’d finally get rid of them after the last dinner party. Yeah, I remember her saying she’d “sort it out” last year. But I guess she’s been too busy with work and the house renovations to actually do anything about it. I think it’s more about sentimentality than practicality. A lot of these pieces were handed down through generations. I remember my gran using the same fork as my great-grandma. It’s got a history. That’s true. I used to collect all sorts of old things when I was younger, just to keep them around. You know, like that one turkey carved by my father in the 70s. Still hangs on the wall above the fireplace. Oh, the turkey! I remember that. It’s got such a weird expression, like it’s judging us all. Maybe we should get a new set, you know, for the sake of the house looking fresh. I’d say go for it, but you have to remember, some things aren’t meant to be replaced. They’ve seen better days, but they’ve also seen us through good and bad times. That’s a good point, Dad. Maybe we could just update the table setting a bit—like new plates or a new set of knives—but keep the old cutlery as a family heirloom. I like that idea. Keep the tradition but update the look. It’ll feel like a fresh start, but with a connection to the past. Exactly. I still use the old tin opener from when I was a kid. It’s not perfect, but it’s reliable. I guess it’s all about balance. The house is changing, but some things should stay the same. You’re both young and full of energy, but remember, nostalgia has its place. Don’t throw out the baby with the bathwater. Right, I’ll talk to Mum about it tomorrow. I’ll propose the idea and see what she says. That sounds like a plan. And if she’s still resisting, we can always have a family vote—like the one we had about the garden. Ha! I remember that. We ended up choosing the cheapest option just to keep the peace. It’s all in the spirit of family, isn’t it?

I just got the confirmation email for our skiing trip. It’s all set for next month. I think it’s going to be a great break from the usual routine. Really? That’s fantastic! I can’t wait. When are we going exactly? The flight leaves on the 12th, so we’ll be on the snow by the 15th. It should be a nice time of year too — not too cold, and the slopes should be in good condition. Sounds perfect! I was worried the weather might be bad, but I guess it’s not too late to check. I’ve already checked with the travel agent, and they said the forecast looks good. They even mentioned there might be some fresh powder in the mountains. I’m really looking forward to it. Oh, I love the idea of fresh powder! I can’t wait to get on the slopes. I’ve been wanting to try some advanced runs, but I know I need to practice more. You’ll be fine. I remember how fast you picked it up the last time we went. You’ve got a natural feel for it. Just don’t forget the goggles and the right gear. I’ve got all my stuff packed already. I even found a new pair of skis I think I’ll take with me. They’re light and flexible — perfect for beginners like me. That’s great to hear. I’m also going to bring my old skis. I think they might still be in good shape. I can’t remember the last time I used them. You should try them out again! It’s been years since we last did this. I think it’ll be a fun way to reconnect with the sport. Definitely. I know I’m going to need the extra practice, but it’ll be nice to get back into the rhythm. Speaking of which, have you been working hard lately? You look a bit tired. Yeah, I’ve been busy at work. I’m still on my feet most of the day, and I haven’t had much time to myself. I’m looking forward to some rest and relaxation. Then this trip is exactly what you need. Just make sure you don’t overdo it once we get there. We’ll have time to explore, ski, and just enjoy the fresh air.

I can't believe we've got another exam tomorrow. I’ve been studying non-stop for the past two days, and I still feel like I haven’t learned anything. I know, right? I was doing the same thing last night. I even had to ask my mum for help with my Spanish homework. She tried to explain the verb tenses, but I just got more confused. I wish we could just take a break and watch some of those documentaries we were talking about earlier. Yeah, I’d love that. But I also think we need to focus on our future. Have you thought about what you want to do after school? I heard about this new food tech program at the local college. It’s supposed to be really cool and combine science with cooking. Maybe we could both apply? That sounds amazing! I’ve always loved cooking, and I also think it would be way more interesting than sitting in a classroom all day. What about you? Are you thinking about anything specific? Honestly, I’m still not sure. I guess I’m too scared to commit to anything. I just want to make sure I’m good at all the subjects before I even start thinking about college. Plus, I’m still trying to decide if I want to take Spanish or maybe even learn another language. I get that. I’ve been thinking about taking another language too. I mean, it’s a requirement for most college courses, right? And it’s kind of fun. I’ve been practising with my phone app every night. It’s not too bad, honestly. That’s a good idea. Maybe we could study together sometimes. I’ve been struggling with some of the grammar stuff, and I know you’re better at it than I am. For sure! I’d love to. We could even make it a weekly thing. Just like old times.

So, I've been meaning to ask you, have you seen the new film by that director, like... the one with the haunted house and the twins? I think it came out last week. I tried to watch it, but honestly, I couldn't get past the first half-hour. It was too slow and all the characters were so... dull.      Oh, I saw it! I actually really liked it. I know it's not everyone's cup of tea, but I found the pacing deliberate. It wasn't just slow for the sake of it. It gave the story time to build, you know? And the twins' dynamic was really interesting. They had such a complicated relationship.      Hmm, I guess I just got bored. I mean, I’m not the biggest fan of horror, and I think the whole thing felt like it was trying too hard to be scary. I mean, the soundtrack was so ominous, but the acting was... I don’t know, not enough.      I thought the acting was pretty good, actually. The lead, the one who plays the twin with the dark past, did a fantastic job. It’s not the kind of role you’d normally cast for, but she brought so much depth to it.      Yeah, I suppose. I just felt like there were too many plot twists that didn’t really add up. Like, why did the twin kill the other one? It didn’t make sense. I mean, I get that they were trying to show the psychological aspects, but it felt a bit forced.      I didn’t think it was forced. I thought it was a deliberate choice to make the audience question the reality of the story. It’s one of those films where you’re not sure if you’re watching a horror movie or a psychological thriller. Maybe that’s the point.      Well, I’ll admit, I might have missed something. I did fall asleep halfway through, though. I tried to stay awake, but I just couldn’t. Maybe I’ll try again.      Oh, you should! I think you’d really like it if you give it a second chance. I’m going to see it again this weekend with some friends. It’s a great film to discuss, actually.      Alright, I’ll consider it. Maybe after I finish watching  The Midnight Adventure  on DVD.      You’ll regret that, I promise.

It’s a beautiful morning, isn’t it? I think it’s been like this all week—just perfect weather for a walk or something. Yes, it’s been quite nice. I even thought about going for a walk in the park, but I ended up just staying in with a good book and some tea. You know how it is. I can imagine. I’ve been thinking about starting to run again. I’ve had this idea of joining a local running group. I heard they meet every Saturday morning, and the weather has been so good lately. That sounds lovely. I used to run when I was younger. It was my way of keeping fit and staying in shape. You should try it. It’s a great way to meet people too, and it keeps you active. I’d love that. I just need to get myself into the habit. I’ve been a bit lazy lately, what with the work and everything. You know how it is. Also, I’ve been thinking about starting a new project with my students—maybe something related to literature or something that could inspire them. That sounds exciting. I always thought you had a brilliant way with words. You could inspire all sorts of people. I remember when I was at school, my English teacher was just like you—always had us reading great books and thinking deeply about them. Oh, you were lucky. I mean, I was someone who found it hard to get excited about literature sometimes. It just wasn’t my thing. But you were always the one who loved the stories and the characters. Well, I think it’s a shame if you don’t find a way to bring that passion back. You have so much to offer. Maybe you could even write something. I’d love to read a story from you one day. I might just do that. I’ve been thinking about it a lot lately. But I need to get my head straight first. I’ve been getting distracted by too many things—work, money, even driving lessons. I’ve been meaning to take them for ages now. You should do it. Driving is a skill that’s important, especially if you plan on doing more things like running or going out. I had to take it myself when I was younger. It was a bit of a hassle, but it was worth it.

I can’t believe we actually made it through the whole week without going mad. I think the only thing that kept me going was the thought of getting home and having a proper meal. Yeah, I felt the same. I honestly couldn’t tell you what we had for dinner yesterday—it just all blurred together. But I’m glad we made it. I was starting to think we were going to have to take a break and go to a takeaway just to survive. Oh, don’t even get me started. I was considering that. I think I might have called a Thai place the other day just to get something edible. But then I thought, "Wait, we’re still in China, not London." It’s like the food here is just… different. I miss the convenience of just walking into a shop and grabbing something quick. I know, right? It’s not that the food is bad, it’s just that it’s not the same. I was in a market the other day and saw these amazing little buns, but they looked so small. I thought, "Wait, is that even enough for one meal?" It was a bit of a struggle. I remember when we first came here, I was so confused. I tried to buy a loaf of bread and ended up with a whole bag of something that looked like rice. It took me a while to realize that wasn’t bread. I think I still have that bag in my flat. Oh, I remember that. You were so excited about it, thinking it was a new kind of bread. I tried to explain it was just a different type of grain. But you weren’t having it. You were too scared to try it. It was hilarious. I still can’t get over how much work it is to buy even the simplest things. I mean, I have to check labels, read instructions, and sometimes I just end up giving up and ordering something from the app. It’s not the same as just walking into Tesco and grabbing a bag of chips. I agree. I think we’re going to have to start planning our shopping trips more carefully. I mean, we can’t keep doing this. We need to figure out where the best places are and maybe get a routine going.

I just finished reading this lovely book about baking, and I thought we could try one of the recipes this weekend. It’s got these amazing chocolate chip scones that are supposed to be perfect with a cup of tea. Yum! That sounds like fun! I love baking with you, Mom. I think I can help you with the scones. I got really good at mixing things in my kitchen. Yeah, I can help too! I’m pretty good with my hands, and I like to help you cook. I think I can even decorate the scones with some sugar shapes. Can I come with you? I want to see your friends too. I’ve been wanting to meet them since you told me about them last week. That’s a great idea, but I need to check with your dad first. I don’t want to overbook us. I’m also going to see if I can get a haircut on Friday. My hair is getting a bit too long, and I want it to look good for the photoshoot we’re planning. They need a few photos of people doing different things, and they’re asking me to be one of the models. I’m a bit nervous, but it sounds fun. That sounds cool! I want to be in one too! Can I be part of it? Definitely! I’ll make sure to tell them about you. I just have to get the details sorted with the person organizing it. Oh, and I was wondering if we could go to the park on Sunday. I heard there’s a little market there, and I thought we could maybe buy some fresh fruit for the scones. I like markets! I’ve been wanting to go to one for ages. I can help you pick out the best fruit. Me too! I think I can even help you make the scones. I’ve watched you do it before. That’s the spirit!

So, do you know what’s happening this weekend? I heard there’s a big party at the Student Union. I’m thinking of going out, but I’m not sure if I’ll be up for it after the midterms. Oh, I heard about that too! I think it’s on Saturday night. I was going to go, but I got stuck with some group project stuff all week. Maybe I’ll go later in the week? I mean, I don’t want to miss out on the vibes. Yeah, the vibes are always worth it. Although, I’m still trying to figure out what to wear. I don’t want to look like a total cliché, you know? Like, that black t-shirt and jeans combo that everyone wears. Oh, I get you. You know, I once tried to go out in matching skinny jeans and a hoodie, and I got stared at like I was a total weirdo. I still don’t know if that was the best idea. Ha, I can imagine. I once wore a shirt that said “I heart uni” and had to explain it to every single person I met. It was like a horror movie. Anyway, what are you having for lunch? I grabbed a sandwich and a coffee from the canteen. Same here, actually. I had a chicken wrap and a smoothie. The smoothie was like, the worst thing I’ve ever tasted. It tasted like a mix of spinach and something that wasn’t supposed to be in a smoothie. Oh no, that’s not good. And to the family who makes it possible.      And to the family who doesn’t make it possible, but still manages to feed us anyway.      This is good. Proper meat, not that pre-prepped stuff you get in shops these days.      Aye, and the vegetables are fresh too. I’ve been to those fancy supermarkets, you know. Everything’s so shiny, but it doesn’t taste right.      You know, being a lecturer, I’ve had a lot of fancy dinners. But I still miss the real thing.      And what’s the real thing without the people to share it with?      Aye, that’s right. I used to work, but now I’m just here, enjoying the company and the food.      It’s funny, isn’t it? We’re all retired now, and we still find ways to keep the old habits alive.      And the old traditions. Even if we’ve got postgraduate degrees, we still love our Sunday roasts.      And we still have the same taste for a good pie and a pint.      To the old traditions, and the new ones we make together.      To family, food, and the things that make life worth living.      To the warmth of home and the laughter of those we love.      And to the next Sunday roast.      I reckon we’ll be doing this for a long time yet.      Aye, and I’m not going to be the one to stop it.      You’re not going to stop anything. You’re too busy eating.      And too busy enjoying the company of the best people in the world.      Aye, that’s the truth.      And that’s what makes this place special.      It’s not just the food. It’s the love in it.

I can't believe how much food we've got here! It's like a feast for the whole week. Mum’s got this massive lasagna in the oven, and Dad’s making a huge pot of soup. Yeah, I know, it’s like she’s been preparing for a party or something. I mean, she’s always been a bit of a foodie, but this is taking it to a whole new level. Oh, don’t be so surprised. It’s not like she hasn’t done this before. I remember when I was a kid, she used to cook every Sunday like it was a holy day. And the lasagna? And when she wasn’t cooking, she was telling stories about her own childhood—like how she learned to cook from her mum, who used to make a mean stew. Ah, stories, yes. I remember those. She used to make these insane cakes with tons of layers and stuff. My sister even once got engaged at her house because the cake was so good. Oh, I remember that! It was a vanilla sponge with chocolate icing and a candle on top. She told the story about it for years. Said it was the most perfect cake she’d ever made. She did have a point. It was a real cake, not just a birthday decoration. And it was  good . I still remember the smell of it when it came out of the oven. Made me miss my mum’s cooking, even though she was a terrible baker.

I've been thinking a lot about how to integrate more interactive learning into university courses. You know, like using VR or some kind of gamified platform. I’m trying to make it more engaging for students who are used to scrolling through TikTok or watching viral videos. That actually sounds really interesting. I mean, I've seen how much students are glued to their phones, even in class. Maybe if we designed modules that feel like a game or a social challenge, they’d be more motivated to participate. Exactly! And it’s not just about making it fun. It's about making sure the content is accessible to all students. I've been working with a start-up that uses AI to personalize learning paths based on a student’s interests and performance. It's pretty cutting-edge, honestly. That sounds like a great idea. I think the key is to make education feel less like a lecture and more like a journey. I remember when I was teaching, a few students used to ask, “Why is this even relevant?” If we can answer that, we might actually change how students engage with their studies. I agree. I’ve been talking with a few entrepreneurs about how to apply these strategies on a larger scale. It’s not just about the tools; it's about the mindset. How can we shift the culture in universities to be more student-centered and flexible? Definitely. It’s not just about the technology; it's about how we use it. For example, I once had a student who was really into gaming. When I let him design a project around a video game concept, his engagement level skyrocketed. It worked because it tapped into his passion. That’s a perfect example. I think we should encourage more project-based learning, especially in subjects that are often seen as dry. Maybe even integrate social media or platforms like TikTok as a way for students to share their work and get feedback from peers. I love that. It could open up a whole new world of collaboration. I mean, imagine if students could pitch their ideas on a platform and get real-time feedback from experts or even other students around the world. That’s the kind of innovation we need in education. Exactly. I think it’s time for universities to rethink their approach.

I can’t believe it’s already October. I feel like we just had the first day of autumn. Have you seen the leaves out there? They’re all golden and red now. I heard a funny joke about pumpkins the other day, something about how they’re not just for Halloween. They’re actually for everything! I love that kind of humor. I want to work on some projects with my colleagues, maybe even start my own team if the opportunity comes up. That sounds like a great plan. I hope things go well for you.

I just got a call from my cousin in Manchester. She said they’re planning a family reunion in the summer. I think it’s about time we all got together again. That does sound nice. I can’t believe we’re in France and we’re still talking about uni stuff. I mean, it’s like we got here and then immediately switched back to our old lives. Yeah, I know, it’s weird. I feel like I should be speaking French or something, but I can’t even say “bonjour” properly. It’s like my brain’s on autopilot. You’re not the only one. I said “merci, please” and the guy at the café just stared at me like I was speaking Martian. I was so embarrassed. I should’ve just said “no” and then left. But I was too scared to make a bigger mistake. Hey, maybe we could start learning some French together. I mean, we’re both students, and we’re in France. It’d be like a fun project. That sounds cool. I could even teach you some English slang. You know, like “cheers” or “mate.” Oh, I’d love that. I’m pretty sure I could pick up a few phrases just by listening to you. Though I’m not sure if “cheers” is even used in France. I don’t know. Maybe in some areas. But I think it’s more like “merci.” I’m still confused about the difference. Exactly! I mean, we’re talking about translating between languages and we’re still getting confused. I think I need to take a language class. Maybe you should. I’ve been thinking about taking a French course too. Maybe we could do it together. That’s an idea. We could study and then practice by talking to people here. It’d be a good way to mix our uni work with some real-life experience. Yeah, I like that. And who knows, maybe we’ll even pick up some local bands or something. I heard there are some great indie groups here. I’d love to check some out. Maybe we could go to a concert? It’d be a great way to explore the city and brush up on our French. Deal. I’ll text you some local spots. And maybe even ask someone if they know any good places to find music. Perfect. I’m excited.

I just found a spider in the kitchen this morning. I couldn’t believe it—this one was huge! I thought I was dreaming at first. You know how some people say they can see spiders in the corners of their eyes? Oh, I know what you mean. I had a spider in my bathroom last week. I was scrubbing the tiles and saw this big one scuttling across the wall. I froze for a moment. I didn’t move, just stared at it. I thought it might be a sign or something. You're not the only one who gets spooked by them. I remember when I was a kid, my mother used to say spiders were good luck. But I always thought she was just trying to scare me off the garden. She used to say, "If you catch a spider, bring it inside. It'll bring you luck." That sounds like something my gran would say. I used to believe that too. But honestly, the only good thing about spiders is that they keep the mice away. I’ve had more than one mouse invasion in my flat. Yeah, I’ve had that too. A few years ago, I found a mouse nest in the airing cupboard. It was like a little village! I was so disgusted. I ended up calling a pest control company. I didn’t want to deal with it myself. It’s not just spiders and mice. I’ve had birds in my flat too. A sparrow once flew through the window and landed on the kitchen counter. I thought it was going to fly away, but it just sat there staring at me like it knew something I didn’t. That’s funny. I had a bird once—well, not a real bird, but a plastic one. I bought it for my son’s birthday. He used to play with it, but then he outgrew it. I kept it on the shelf for years. I even named it Bubbles. Oh, that’s adorable. I used to have a little figurine of a bird too. It was a handmade one from a craft market. I still have it on my mantelpiece. It’s been there for over ten years. I like that. It gives the place character. You know, I think our homes are like stories—each one has its own characters, whether they’re real or not.

I just wanted to say how lovely it is to see you again. It’s been ages since we last met. I’ve been meaning to get in touch, but things have been so busy with work and everything. Oh, it’s so good to see you too. I can’t believe how quickly time has flown. I’ve been meaning to visit you in Stevenage for ages. It’s been a while since we’ve sat down and caught up properly. She had Alzheimer’s, and it was a slow, painful process. I’m so sorry to hear that. I can only imagine what that’s been like for you. I lost my grandmother to the same disease a few years back, and it was heartbreaking. It changed our whole family dynamic. Yes, it really did. I’ve been trying to document her life and the stories she used to tell. It’s strange to think she’s not here anymore, but I still feel her presence in so many ways. That’s a beautiful way to remember her. I’ve been helping my family with their family tree too. It’s amazing how much of our heritage we’ve been able to uncover. It’s also been a way to connect with our roots. That sounds like a meaningful project. I’ve always been interested in family history, even though I never got much of a chance to explore it fully.

I just saw the most incredible sight today. You remember that old field we passed on our way here? Well, there were these massive hot air balloons floating over the hills. I’ve never seen such a thing in the countryside. Oh, I remember. You were so excited about it. I thought it was just a few balloons, but then I realized there were like eight or nine of them. They were all different colors, and they looked like they were part of some kind of festival. It was like a floating carnival. I mean, imagine being up there, right above the trees and the fields. I could hardly believe my eyes. I’ve always loved the idea of hot air ballooning, but I never thought I’d see it in such a peaceful setting. I know, it was beautiful. It reminded me of the time we went camping in the Lake District and saw the sunrise from the top of a hill. The way the light hit the balloons was like something out of a dream. Speaking of which, have you been thinking about that camping trip again? I was just telling my sister about how I’ve been saving up for a small trip with some friends. It’s only a few hundred pounds, but it’d be nice to get out of the city for a while. I’d love that. I’ve been feeling like I need a break. I’ve been working way too much lately. Maybe we could go together? You know, just the two of us, out in the wild. That sounds perfect. It would be nice to get away from the noise of London for a bit. I’ve been missing the countryside lately. Plus, I’ve been thinking about getting a dog. I finally saved up enough for a small one. A dog? You’re not serious. You’d have to take care of it, feed it, walk it. What kind of dog are you thinking about getting? A small breed, maybe a terrier or something. I love the idea of having a pet to keep me company. We could even take it camping. Though I’m not sure how well it’d do with the wildlife. Yeah, I’d be worried about the power lines near the campsite. I’ve seen so many birds getting tangled up in them. I think it’s a real problem in the countryside.

I just love this time of year. The weather's been so unpredictable lately—it's like the seasons are having a conversation with themselves. I swear, it’s like spring and autumn are trying to take over in the same week. I know, I know—some days it’s warm enough to wear a sweater, and the next day it’s freezing. It’s like the weather’s got a grudge against us. Exactly! I’ve been thinking about how much easier it would be if we could just control the weather. Maybe we could have a class on that—how to influence the seasons? Though I’m not sure if it would be a language class or a meteorology one. You’d probably have to teach it in a different language though. I’ve tried learning Spanish, but I still can’t get the past tense right. It’s like the language is fighting back. Ha! I’ve been teaching English to adults for years, and I’ll tell you, the past tense is one of the hardest things for them to grasp. One of my students thought "I went to the gym" meant he was still there. I had to explain it was like a memory. That sounds like a classic teaching moment. I’ve always wondered how you manage to keep it so engaging. I mean, I’m not even sure I could teach a language, let alone keep people interested in it. It helps when you’re passionate about it. And, honestly, people love learning about the language they speak. I often tell them that the key to language learning is not just memorizing vocabulary, but understanding the culture behind it. That’s true. I’ve always thought that about work as well. You can’t just manage people by giving orders—you have to understand their motivations. I’ve learned that the hard way. I remember when I started teaching, I had this idea that if I was strict, people would respect me. But now I realize that it’s about building trust. Speaking of trust, have you been to the gym in Solihull? I heard they’ve been doing some new coaching techniques. Yeah, I’ve been meaning to check it out. I think they’ve introduced some virtual classes. It’s a bit of a buzzword now—interactive fitness. I’m not sure if I’m ready for that yet, but I’d love to see how it works.

Right, I’ve got everything we need for the week. But let me check again—did we get the chicken?      Yeah, I saw the chicken in the fridge. Just need to take it out when we’re cooking. But I don’t think we need to buy more eggs. We’ve got enough for a few days.      Oh, I brought the paper. You know, I read once that Yorkshire has the best chicken in the country. Though I suppose it’s just as good as anywhere else.      You know what they say—Yorkshire chicken, Yorkshire weather, and Yorkshire’s got the best of both. Though I do love a good bit of bubble and squeak when it’s cold out.      That’s the spirit! And speaking of food, I was thinking, maybe we can have a little get-together this weekend. I even found a copy of  The White Album  in the attic. Though I have to say, I think the younger generation still prefers streaming.      That’s true. But there’s something special about vinyl. You can hear the music better, and the smell of the records is like a memory all on its own.      Well, I’ll have to check the budget. I can’t believe we've got another 20 miles to go. I thought the satnav said it was only 15. Maybe it’s wrong again. I swear, these things are more confused than a first-time driver. Oh, come on! You know how unreliable those satnavs are. I remember once I followed one to the middle of a forest. My wife had to call a helicopter to get me out. It was a mess. Oh, don’t remind me. I don’t know, I’m just not a big fan of getting lost or delayed. Especially when I’ve got a gig to get to. I get it. We’re both the type to plan things out. I think it’s part of being a writer and a teacher. You’ve got to be organized.

So, did you get the project brief for the university building? I was reading through it this morning and it’s a real gem. I just made a fresh pot of tea. You know, I always say it's the best way to start the day, and I think it’s the best way to start catching up with someone I care about. Yeah, I couldn’t agree more. I’ve tried to plan my routes better, but it’s still a challenge. I can imagine. I’ve been thinking about how to make our social plans work around the traffic, though.

I just got an email from the BBC about a media job. They’re looking for someone with experience in radio and journalism. I thought you might want to help me with the application, ANON. Oh, that sounds exciting! I’ve seen the ad—some sort of producer role, right? You’re applying for that, aren’t you? Yeah, I am. It’s a bit of a dream come true. I’d be happy to help. First, you need to make sure your CV highlights your relevant experience. You’ve worked with local radio stations before, right? Yes, I did. I was a producer for a few years in Manchester. But I’m not sure if that’s enough. I’ve been thinking about changing careers, so maybe I need to frame it in a way that shows I’m a good fit for this role. That’s a good point. You can mention your experience in news production, your ability to handle live broadcasts, and your teamwork skills. But I’m a bit nervous about the interview. What if they ask me about handling pressure or working in a fast-paced environment? That’s a common question. You should prepare examples of times when you’ve worked under tight deadlines or managed multiple projects at once. You can use the STAR method—Situation, Task, Action, Result. It can show you’re passionate about the industry. If you have any side projects, like podcasting or blogging, that could be a great addition. It shows initiative and a genuine interest in the field. That makes sense. I do have a small podcast where I interview local community members. I think I’ll include that. Thanks for the advice, I feel a bit more confident now. Anytime! You’ve got the skills and the passion.

I've been thinking a lot lately about making a change, you know? I've got this idea for a small business, and I'm not sure if I'm ready to go all in on it yet. I can see why you'd be nervous—starting a business is a big step. But I think you've got the skills and determination to make it work. What's the business idea exactly? I want to open a sustainable café that serves locally sourced coffee and also offers a small workshop space for people to learn basic woodworking or something like that. It's not just about making money; it's about creating a community space. That sounds amazing. I love the idea of combining a café with a workshop. It would be a great way to bring people together. But have you considered the costs and the logistics? I know it’s a lot to take in. I’ve been doing some research and talking to a few people in the local business community. And she used to type out all her stories and poems, just like we do now with computers. Though, I have to say, it was so much slower back then. You had to type every word, and if you made a mistake, you had to start again. Wait, but now we have Excel and all these fancy programs. I think I saw something about it on PlayStation once. Oh, you mean the ones where you can create your own games? I’ve seen some of those. They’re pretty cool, but I still think there’s something special about telling stories out loud, like we did when we were younger. I want to build a castle with LEGO! I saw one in the Brownie Promise evening. It had a moat and a tower. Oh, the Brownie Promise! That was a great event. I remember when I was your age, I had to promise to be kind and help others. It was a bit scary at first, but I really enjoyed it. I liked the part where we had to do the pledge. It felt like I was part of something bigger. I still remember the whole room chanting “I promise to be kind…” It sounded really cool. I think I saw a video of it online. There were all these kids doing the pledge and making promises. It looked really fun. Yeah, it was. And when I think about all the things we did growing up, like playing games and telling stories, it makes me miss those days sometimes. But I love how we can still do those things now with our computers and the internet. I think it’s still the same, though. We just have more ways to do it. Like we can send stories to each other through emails or even make our own games on PlayStation.

I’ve been meaning to ask you, do you still have that old house in the countryside? It’s been ages since we talked about selling it. I’ve been thinking about it ever since I saw that letter about the new development nearby. Oh, you know I’ve been putting it off. It’s one of those things that always seems to be "when I have time," but I never do. Though I do miss the view. You remember how the morning light used to come through the big window and hit the floor like gold? I remember. It was magical, honestly. I still get that feeling sometimes when I’m out walking near the old village. Though I suppose it’s more of a memory now. I’ve been meaning to visit the medieval village nearby, the one that’s almost deserted now. It’s strange, isn’t it? The way history just sits there, waiting to be noticed. Yeah, I thought about that the other day. I was driving past the old farm that used to grow apples, and I remembered how my mum used to make that sort of jam. I’ve been trying to grow some herbs in my garden, but I can’t get the right soil. Maybe I should have asked you for advice? You should have. I’ve been growing some basil and thyme in pots. It’s not much, but it’s enough for tea and a bit of cooking. Oh, and I’ve been trying to cut down on junk mail. I mean, what’s the point? I just throw it all in the bin. Can you believe the number of letters we get about roadworks? I’m tired of seeing signs everywhere. I know. I’ve been meaning to tell you about the time I got a letter about roadworks and found out that the route they were planning was right past my old friend’s house. He’s a bit of a stickler for old buildings, and he was furious. You’d have laughed if you’d seen him. I’d have. I’ve told you about the time I wore those scruffy clothes to a meeting. I thought I looked cool, but I looked like I’d been living in a landfill. You should have seen the looks on their faces. I can just imagine. You were always the one who dressed like a postman in the middle of summer, weren’t you?

I just got a new box of chocolates from the local shop, and I was thinking, maybe we could try them with some wine tonight? It’s been a while since we had a proper evening together. Sounds like a great idea. I’ve been meaning to catch up with you both. I’ve been working late a lot, and I’m starting to feel like I’m losing my edge. Have you noticed anything like that with your work lately? Honestly, I haven’t. It’s been interesting working from home. I’ve got the freedom to set my own hours, but sometimes it’s hard to switch off. I’ve even started using Facebook groups for some work-related projects, which has been both helpful and a bit of a distraction. I can imagine. I’ve been using my mobile phone more for work too, and I think it’s starting to take a toll on my eyes. I’ve been trying to set boundaries, like not checking work emails after 7 PM. It’s not always easy, but I’m getting better at it. That’s admirable. I’ve been trying the same thing, but with my job, it’s a bit trickier. I’ve got a team relying on me, so I can’t always just walk away. Have you ever considered taking a holiday or a short break? I actually did take a short break last month. I went to Brighton and stayed in a guesthouse. It was amazing—so different from the city. I even met someone who works in the hospitality industry. We talked about travel and how to plan a trip without breaking the bank. That sounds lovely. I’ve been thinking about taking a trip too, maybe to Norfolk. I’ve always wanted to visit the coast, and the weather’s finally starting to get better. Maybe we could plan something together? That would be great. I’ve heard great things about Norfolk. I’ve got a friend who lives there, and she’s always talking about the local cafes and the fresh seafood. If you’re up for it, I could help you plan the trip. I’d love that. I’ll start looking up some travel blogs and see what’s on offer. Oh, and I’ve got this idea for a Christmas present—maybe go for something handmade? I know you both like supporting local businesses.

So, how’s the new job going? You mentioned you were going to start part-time programming for the survey company last week. Oh, it’s going alright, I suppose. It’s a bit of a steep learning curve, but the boss is pretty laid-back. I’m getting used to writing code for the surveys, which is a bit different from what I studied at uni. That’s cool. I bet it’s more practical than your postgrad work? Honestly, it’s not that different. I mean, I did a master’s in data science, so I was already familiar with some of the tools. But it’s nice to see how the theories apply in real life. My lectures were all about models and algorithms, but here, I’m actually building things from scratch. I can imagine. I mean, I used to write copy for ads, so I was always trying to find clever ways to say things. It’s kind of the same idea, just with code instead of words. Yeah, I guess so. It’s just, you know, working with data feels more like solving a problem every day. I’ve already got a few bugs to fix, but I’m not too bad. You’re a quick learner then. I remember when I first started writing copy, I used to get so frustrated trying to make the message stick. You have to know what the client wants, but also make it sound natural. Sounds like a nightmare. I’d rather code than write ads. I mean, you can’t really argue with a survey result. True, but I guess there’s something satisfying about helping people communicate better. Although I do miss the days when I could just write whatever I wanted. I know what you mean. It’s funny, isn’t it? We’re both in the creative world, even if one of us is coding and the other is writing. Exactly. So, what about you? You said you’re thinking about moving back to Oxford for a while. Are you planning to take that job full-time next year? Yeah, I think so. I’ve got an offer for a full-time position there, and I figure if I stay in London too long, I’ll just end up paying rent for a place I never actually live in. That’s smart. I’ve been thinking about moving back to Kent, actually.

So, I've been thinking about getting back into exercise. I've been feeling a bit sluggish lately. I used to go running every morning, but I haven’t had the time or motivation lately. What do you think, Elise?      I can relate. I haven’t been exercising much either. I’ve been so caught up with work and trying to manage the household. But I think I need to get back into some kind of routine. Maybe I can start with a few short walks around the neighborhood?      I know what you mean. I’ve been trying to get back into my writing routine, but I also need to take care of my health. I’ve started doing some yoga and light stretching in the mornings. It helps me feel more centered and gives me energy throughout the day. You should try it, it’s not too hard and it’s very calming.      Yoga sounds good. I’ve never been into it much, but maybe I could give it a go. I’m not sure I have the space at home, though. The house is a bit cramped, and I don’t want to take up too much room.      I actually have a small mat in the hallway. I use it when I’m waiting for the kettle to boil or when I need a quick break. It’s not much, but it works. Maybe you could set up something similar? You don’t need a large space, just a clear area.      Exactly. I think it’s more about the consistency than the space. Even a few minutes a day can make a difference. Plus, it’s a great way to clear your mind before starting the day. I’ve been finding that I’m more productive when I do it.      That makes sense. I need to be more disciplined. I’ve been lazy about a lot of things lately. But I do feel like I need to take better care of myself. Speaking of which, have you heard anything about the house prices around here? I’ve been thinking about buying a place, but the market is so volatile.      I've heard the same thing. It’s been quite unpredictable. Some areas are going up, others are stable or even decreasing. I think it's still a bit early to make a big decision, but I've been keeping an eye on a few properties.

I can't believe the Budget’s out. You know, I was just thinking about it on my way here. It feels like every time there's a new policy, it's just another tax hike or another cut to public services. Yeah, I heard about it on the train. It’s pretty rough on people like us, especially with the cost of living going up every year. I’ve been trying to keep my expenses down, but with the inflation rate as high as it is, it’s really tough. I know, it's like the government just keeps throwing money at the wrong things. I saw a report about how even small businesses are struggling. I mean, I work in administration, but I still feel like the system is stacked against people like me. I agree, but I guess it's a bit of a sad state of affairs. I'm thinking of moving to Germany eventually, just for a bit. I’ve been working on some projects there for a while, and I hear the economy is more stable, even if it's not perfect. That’s interesting. I’ve always wanted to visit Germany, but I never thought about moving there. I’ve got this friend who works as an engineer in Munich, and he says the job market is pretty good. But I’m not sure if I’d want to move away from family, you know? Yeah, family’s important. But then again, sometimes you have to make tough choices for your future. I mean, I've been thinking about my own career path. I was a graduate civil engineer, so I guess I’m still in that field. But I’m looking at some opportunities in sustainable energy projects. That sounds cool. I mean, I’ve always been interested in the environment, even if I didn’t know much about the technical side of it. I’ve been thinking about doing a course in environmental policy, maybe after I finish my current job. It’s something I’ve always wanted to pursue, but the timing just never worked out. That’s a great idea. I could see you really getting into that. You’ve always had a good eye for detail, and you’re really good with numbers. It’s no surprise you’re a graduate now. Thanks, I guess. But I still feel like the system isn’t really giving people like us the chance to move up.

You know, I’ve been thinking about the changes in the neighborhood. The council’s got this big plan to redevelop the area, and I can’t help but feel like we’re losing something special. Not to mention the sound of all those construction sites. I know what you mean. I’ve been driving through all that noise for a week now. It’s like they’re trying to build a whole new city instead of just fixing what’s already there. But you know what? I’ve always said that Liverpool’s soul is in its streets, not its skyscrapers. Exactly! And I’ve been thinking about how people are moving away because of the noise and the mess. It’s not just about the buildings; it’s about the community. I mean, I’ve been lecturing about urban development for years, and I still don’t think we’ve got it right. Haha, you sound like you’re writing a thesis. But you know, I’ve seen a lot of change since I was a kid. When I first started driving, this area was practically deserted. Now, it’s packed with new shops and apartments. It’s a bit sad, really. I remember when we used to have that old cinema on the corner. I used to go there all the time when I was growing up. Now it’s just a boarded-up building. Yeah, I remember that. There was this one film that came out back in the ‘90s—some action movie with a British actor. I still remember the poster. It was way more exciting than the stuff they show now. I agree about the films. I think the acting’s gotten better, but the stories have gone down a bit. I mean, it’s easier to make a film now, but it’s harder to make something that connects with people. That’s why I started taking acting classes. It’s a new goal in life—maybe something to do when I retire. You’re getting somewhere with that. I’ve been thinking about starting up a small business. Maybe a second-hand shop. I’ve been picking up some good stuff from the market, and I’ve got a few friends who might want to buy or sell. That sounds like a solid plan. You’ve always been good at knowing what people need.

I can't believe we've been on the road for three days already. I was hoping it would feel like a holiday, but I'm starting to feel like I'm stuck in a time loop. I know, it's been a bit of a grind, but the view out the window keeps me going. I mean, look at the mountains—it's like we’re moving through a painting. A painting? I would have called it a surreal dream. But I’m not sure I like the idea of hitchhikers we’ve seen on the way. I mean, they looked like they were just waiting to jump in. I know, and I felt the same. It's like everyone’s trying to get somewhere faster than we are. I almost tried to flag one down, but I thought it would be safer to stick to the plan. Yeah, safety first. I still can’t believe I’m driving a campervan in Eastern Europe. I didn’t think I’d ever get to this point. I mean, I was unemployed for years—just surviving on savings, and now here I am, driving across Europe with a friend. It’s wild, isn’t it? I mean, I always thought I’d be the one with the job, the stable income, but I’m not. I’m just a teacher, and even that feels like a stretch these days. I get that. I’ve been through the same thing. I was in education for a while, but it just wasn’t working out. I mean, what’s the point of a degree if you can’t use it? Exactly. And it’s not about the money, though I’ll be honest, it helps. I mean, I can’t afford to travel like this without that extra income. Right, but I think we’re both proving that it’s possible to survive without a traditional career. I just wish more people could see that. I know. It’s about mindset. I mean, I’ve had friends who’ve given up on work and taken up odd jobs, and they’ve told me the same thing: it’s not about what you do, it’s about how you live. That’s true. I guess we’re just trying to clear the clutter, you know? Get rid of the expectations and just live what we want.

I can't believe we've been on the road for almost an hour. I thought it would take less time. Did you check the map again? I did, and I thought we’d be there by now. But with all the train strikes and roadworks, it’s like the whole country’s in chaos. I hope we don’t end up missing the Hay Festival this year. Oh, you’ve got to be joking! That’s the first thing you think of? We’re going to the shops, not to some literary gala. Although, I must say, the Hay Festival is amazing. I remember when I was a kid, my dad used to take me there every year. He’d read me stories from the best authors, and I’d fall asleep in the middle of it. Probably because I was too tired from all the books and stories he’d read me at night. That sounds lovely. I wish I had that kind of experience. I’ve always loved stories, especially fairy tales. I remember once, my mom told me a story about a girl who found a magic key that opened a door to a hidden world. It was so exciting that I actually went to sleep with the story in my head, and I dreamed about it all night. Oh, that’s so sweet. Stories can really capture your imagination. I think that’s why I ended up studying literature at university. It was the only thing that made sense to me after all those years of dealing with the madness of the business world. And yet, here you are, still talking about books. You never really grew up, did you? I mean, it’s not like you’ve had a proper career or anything. I’ve been working in customer services for over twenty years now, and I still have to deal with people who don’t know how to use a vending machine. Maybe that’s the point, though. Life’s too short not to love what you do. I just hope I can go to university soon. I’ve got my GCSEs next month, and I’m hoping to get into a sixth form college. I’ve been studying so hard, and I really want to do well. That’s great, honey. You’ve got a lot of potential. Just go for it. And if you need help with anything, don’t hesitate to ask.

Well, I've just got back from the shops, and I was trying to buy some cleaning products. I got to the end of the aisle, and there was this sign saying, “Clearance: All items 50% off.” I thought, “Oh, brilliant, I can get a bargain!” I grabbed the first thing I saw—a bottle of bleach. I paid, and when I got home, I realized I had bought a bottle of  ketchup . I thought, “What on earth was I thinking?”      Oh, that’s funny! I’ve been there too. I once went to a sale and bought a dress that was supposed to be “black” and came home to find it was more of a “dark brown.” I tried to return it, but the shop said, “We don’t take returns on color mismatches.”      You’re both so dramatic. I just bought a jacket online and it didn’t fit. I thought, “Well, it’s a jacket, right?” But when I tried it on, it was like wearing a wall. My mum said I looked like a tent.      A tent? That’s not very flattering. I’ve been thinking about mental health lately. I saw a documentary about it the other day, and it made me realize I’ve been feeling down for a while. I don’t know if it’s just getting older or something else.      That’s serious. I’ve had some friends who’ve been dealing with depression. It’s not just feeling sad—it’s like being stuck in a fog. You can’t see the way out. If you ever feel like that, you should talk to someone.      Like who? My dad says if you’re feeling down, just take a walk. But I don’t know if that works. Maybe I should try something like that.      Well, it’s better than nothing. I’ve also been thinking about clearing out my old stuff. I’ve been meaning to sort through my attic for years. It’s full of things from when I was a kid.      That’s a good idea. I remember when I was a kid, my mum had this thing about getting rid of stuff. She’d say, “If you don’t use it, you don’t need it.” But I’m not sure I agree. Some of my old toys have sentimental value.      You can’t really get rid of your old toys.

So, mate, I’ve been trying to get my new laptop to work properly, and it’s like it’s got a mind of its own. I think it might be a hardware issue, but I’m not sure. You know how I’ve been gaming a bit more lately, so I thought I’d finally upgrade.      Yeah, I know what you mean. I had that same problem with my last laptop. It would randomly crash when I was working on editing videos. It was a nightmare. Did you try running any diagnostics?      You know, I had a similar issue with my old computer. It was so slow, I couldn’t even load YouTube without it freezing. I ended up having to take it to a local tech store. They said it was the hard drive, and I had to replace it.      That’s what I’m afraid of. I’ve been trying to run some basic programs, and it keeps crashing. Maybe I should check if the drivers are up to date?      You should definitely try that. Also, maybe try running a virus scan. I’ve heard that sometimes malware can cause weird behavior like that.      Or maybe it’s just the laptop itself. I mean, I remember my old one was a bit of a mess, but it worked fine until I had to replace the motherboard. You know what they say—old hardware, new problems.      Haha, yeah. But I’m not ready to give up just yet. I’ve got some stuff I need to work on, like editing some photos and video. I don’t want to get stuck again.      You’re not alone. I still use my old laptop for basic stuff, and it works fine. But I know I need to replace it soon. Maybe I’ll do that next year.      Yeah, I can tell you one thing—technology is a pain in the neck, but it’s necessary. I mean, I can’t even imagine working without a computer these days.      I guess that’s the price of being an artworker. You need all the tools. But honestly, I wish there was a way to just get rid of all the tech nonsense.      Mate, that’s the dream. But until then, we’ve got to make do. Maybe you can try using a different browser? Sometimes that helps with those kinds of issues.      Or maybe you can try connecting it to a monitor or something.

I can’t believe we’re actually here, in Tarnow. I mean, it’s such a different vibe from back home. I’ve never been to Poland before, but this bistro is pretty cool. The interior is modern, and the menu seems… interesting. Yeah, it’s a bit of a contrast, isn’t it? I mean, I grew up in Bury, Lancashire, so I’m used to pubs and cafes that feel like they’ve been around since the 1950s. But this place is like a hybrid of a café and a trendy bar. I love it. I’m still trying to get used to the idea of being in a country that’s not England. Even though I’ve lived in Cambridge for most of my life, I feel like I’m in a different world now. It’s funny how quickly things change, especially when you’re not working. I know what you mean. I used to live in Manchester, and then I moved to London to do my postgrad in English. It’s like every time you move, you feel like you’re starting over. Sometimes I wonder if that’s a sign of something deeper—like a need for change or just… something else. Maybe it’s just the way we’re wired. I’ve always felt like I was waiting for something, like a big shift. I don’t know if it’s age or just the fact that I’ve been unemployed for so long. Sometimes I think about my old job—teaching English. It wasn’t the most glamorous, but it gave me a sense of purpose. I know what you mean. I taught English as a foreign language for a few years. It was hard, but it gave me a way to stay connected with what I love. I still do some part-time work, but it’s not the same as having a full-time role. I’ve been thinking about starting up again. Maybe a small business, something that allows me to stay home but still be productive. I’ve been reading about fitness and self-improvement. It’s strange, but I’ve started going to the gym more often. That’s a great idea. I’ve been trying to get back into fitness too. It helps with the mental health, you know? Sometimes I feel like I’m living between two worlds—my past and my present.

I just got the tickets for the Dorset Steam Fair, and I think we should go this weekend. The weather’s supposed to be nice, and it’s such a great event! Oh, are you sure? I heard it’s a bit of a long day, and the place gets pretty crowded. Plus, I’ve heard some folks say the facilities aren’t the best for people with mobility issues. I think they’ve improved a lot since last year. My cousin has a wheelchair, and she managed to get around just fine. But I agree, it’s always good to check the accessibility before you go. Right, I’ll check the website again and see what they have to say about disabled facilities. I also want to make sure there are shaded areas and enough seating. I’m not a fan of standing around in the sun for hours. That sounds sensible. I still remember when I was younger, I used to drive out there with my mates, and we’d just park somewhere and wander around. But now, with the kids and all, I think it’s better to plan ahead. You’re not the only one. I’ve got a cat who’s getting a bit older, and I’m worried about getting too hot. I’ve been thinking about getting a new sofa anyway—something more comfortable for the both of us. Oh, you’re thinking about moving furniture? I could help you with that. I’ve got a bit of experience with lifting heavy things. Just don’t let me near the cat, though. She’s got a very strong opinion about who can touch her. I heard you’ve got a cat too, didn’t you? I think you mentioned it last week. She’s a bit of a diva, isn’t she? Yeah, she’s got her moments. But she’s got a soft spot for me. I think she’s more interested in my lap than the furniture. That’s not surprising. I’ve always said cats are the best roommates. They’re quiet, they don’t argue, and they’ll keep you company while you’re working. I suppose they’re not bad. I’ve been thinking about getting one too. But I’m not sure I’m ready. I’ve had a few pets in the past, but they all ended up getting too big or too expensive.

Well, I've just got a letter from the council. They say they're moving us out of this house in Kendal. I can't believe it. I've lived here for over fifty years, and now they want me to move? What's the point?      I heard about it, dear. They’ve been talking about redeveloping the area for years. It’s not just you, though. A lot of people in the village are getting letters. But you know, it’s not all bad. We could move to Thirsk. It’s close, and the church has some lovely old houses.      Wait, you’re moving? I thought you were staying for the summer? My mum said you were going to help me with my school project about local history.      Yes, I was, but now this—this is all about the council’s plans. I don’t even know where I’d go. I’ve no friends left in Kendal. I’m quite used to being alone now. And I don’t like change.      I get it, Mum. But maybe it’s not all bad. I’ve been thinking about moving to Thirsk too. It’s a small town, and it’s got a good community. Plus, the arts scene is growing. I’ve been writing a play about local history, and I’d love to have a place where people might actually come to see it.      That's a great idea, Dave. You could maybe audition for the local theatre group. I know the director—she’s very open to new talent. And the community is very supportive. You might even get a chance to perform in front of people who know the area well.      You know, I’ve been thinking about doing something like that too. I’m taking drama at school, and I’d love to get involved. Maybe I could help out with the play?      Well, if you're going to be involved with the performing arts, I suppose I could help you out with the story. I know a lot about the history of this place. I’ve spent my whole life here, you know.      That’d be brilliant, Grandma. You’ve got a real gift for storytelling. I’d love to hear more about the old days. It’s not just about the houses and the land—it’s about the people, the traditions, the stories.

I just got a call from the dentist. They said they want to do a hearing test for Ashaad. He’s been complaining about not hearing properly in one ear, and I think it's probably because of that long time he spent at the library with those headphones on. Is it really necessary? I mean, he’s only six. Why would he need a hearing test? I don’t know, but if he’s got a problem, it’s better to catch it early, isn’t it? Especially if it’s something like that. Didn’t you say he’s been having trouble hearing the teacher at school? Yeah, that’s what the teacher mentioned. He’s missing parts of the lessons, and it’s affecting his concentration. I’m not sure if it’s the headphones or if it’s something else, but the dentist is recommending the test just in case. I guess that makes sense. But why not just get it checked at the GP first? The dentist said they can do the test quickly, and it’s more specialized for things like this. Plus, they mentioned they might refer him to an audiologist if needed. I just hope it’s nothing too serious. Wait, isn’t Ashaad’s birthday coming up? I thought it was the same day as my sister’s. Should we do something special for him? Yes, his birthday is on the same day as your sister’s. We should plan a surprise. Maybe a small party at home? That sounds fun! But what about the school trip? I heard they’re going to a museum this week. I know. I’m trying to get Ashaad to focus on that, but he keeps talking about Monet and the chocolate he saw at Easter. I’m not sure if he’s more excited about the trip or the chocolate. I think he wants both. He told me about the radishes he got from the school garden. He said they were the best ever. Oh, he’s doing a school project on food. He’s really into it. I’m trying to help him with his Maths, but he keeps talking about the radishes instead. Maybe if we tie the radishes into the Maths lesson? Like, calculate how many they need for a recipe or something? That could work. I’ll try that. But first, I need to make sure Ashaad’s hearing is fine.

I can’t believe it’s been a year since we last saw each other! It feels like it’s been forever. What have you been up to? I know, it’s crazy! I’ve been working really hard with the speech and language therapy team at the hospital. It’s been challenging but rewarding. How about you? Still writing copy for that advertising agency? Yeah, still with them. I actually got promoted to lead copywriter a few months ago. It’s a bit overwhelming, but I’m enjoying the creative freedom. I’ve been experimenting with more storytelling in my work lately. You know, like writing more like short narratives rather than just headlines. That sounds cool. I’ve always admired your creativity. I wish I could write like that. It’s funny, I’ve been thinking about how we used to write those silly school stories for our English class back in high school. Remember how we used to make up these crazy adventures for our teachers? Oh, I remember! We used to write about vampires in the school library and pretend we were real. I still have the notebook with all those stories in it. I should take it out and read it again. It’s so nostalgic. Definitely! I still have mine too. So, I was just telling the others about that long cycle ride I did as a child. You know, those summers when we’d all pile into the back of the van with our bikes and head off to the countryside. I've been thinking a lot about how we can use social networking to support the educational initiatives we're planning. I've always believed in the power of education to transform lives, and I think this project has the potential to do just that. Let's make sure we're on the right track and keep refining our ideas as we go.

I just got a message from Lucy. She’s been going through some stuff and said she’s not feeling up to it. I feel awful for her. I’m so glad we’re still in touch after all these years. Yeah, I know. Let’s make sure we all get together. It’s been too long, and I miss those good old days. I think the sea has always been the place where we feel most at home. I couldn’t agree more. The sea has a way of bringing people together. It’s like it calls us back to those simpler times.

I’ve been trying to figure out what’s the  biggest  fashion trend this year, and I’m honestly not sure. It adds personality to an outfit.      Maybe I should try it. I’ve been thinking about going to that local market in Cambridge next weekend. I heard they have a vintage section. I need to see if I can find something that fits my style. What do you think?      Go for it! It’s all about experimenting. You might find something you never knew you liked. And if not, you can always try again next time.

I just got my new camera, Mum. It's a bit fancy, but I think it's going to help me take better pictures of Hastings. You know how I love taking photos of the old buildings? Oh, I know, love. I saw your photos on Instagram. You've got such a good eye. But I have to say, I'm still not sure about that camera. It looks a bit too expensive for a student. But that's what makes you special.

Just come round! I’ve been expecting you ages, Mavis. What kept you?      Sorry, love, I was helping out with a few things at the flat. You know how it is—somebody’s always needing a hand.      Yeah, I know the feeling. I’ve been trying to get that application form sorted for the new job. It’s a bit of a nightmare, honestly.      You always say that. It’s for a managerial position, and I think I’ve missed a few boxes.      I know the feeling. I tried to apply for a childminder course last year, and I still haven’t got the form right.      You’re both missing the point. I think we should just walk to the post office and do it together.      That sounds like a plan. Though I’m not sure I want to deal with the queue.      You’re not the only one. I’ve got a problem with that too. There’s also this issue with the house. The work they did on the roof is absolute shabby.      I know. I told them it was going to be a problem. You can’t even trust the work these days.      I’ve been trying to get some people to help me with the 3D printing project. I thought it might be easier than dealing with construction.      3D printing? That sounds interesting. I heard about it on the telly. You’re making something out of plastic?      Yeah, a little birdhouse. I’m trying to make it look like a real nest.      That sounds lovely. I’ve always liked birds. I used to look after a few when I was younger.      I remember when I was a child, I had a cockerel. He was the best. But he stopped laying eggs when he got too old.      I’ve been trying to get my niece to help me with the birdhouse, but she’s more interested in her phone than the birds.      Yeah, that’s the modern age. I don’t know how you cope with it all.      It’s tough, but we get by. I think we should all go to the post office tomorrow. It’s not like we’re sleeping well anyway.

I've been thinking a lot lately, and I just needed to talk to someone about it. I've been planning to bring my daughter from South Africa to live with me here in Brighton. I've been meaning to ask you, how did you find the job interview the other day? I heard it was for a position in Manchester. Oh, it was a bit nerve-wracking, to be honest.
