I can’t believe we’re actually doing this. Tidying out that cupboard feels like opening a time capsule. I mean, look at this old gardening set—do you remember when we used to pretend we were running a vegetable patch? I think we even tried to grow things in our back garden. Oh, I remember that! We were so serious about it. I think we had a tiny greenhouse made out of old bottles and cardboard. And that plastic watering can—how did we even manage to keep it from leaking? You always ended up watering the cat instead of the plants. That’s right! I still remember the day we tried to plant marigolds. We dug a hole, put the seeds in, and then realized we’d actually just made a hole in the soil. We were so proud, though. It felt like we were in our own little farming empire. And don’t even get me started on the Bako building set. You remember how we used to build those elaborate structures in the shed, even though they never stood up for more than a few minutes? I think we once built a tower that collapsed on your head. I still don’t know how you didn’t get angry. Oh, I was furious at the time! But then we got so wrapped up in the idea of building something that we didn’t mind it falling apart. It was like a competition. It was so much fun, wasn’t it? It was. I think those toys were more than just toys. They were part of who we were. Those memories are so vivid. Even now, looking at them, I can almost feel like we’re kids again, playing with those things in the shed. That’s the thing, isn’t it? We were so young and full of energy. I wonder how different our lives would have been if we’d had the chance to do that kind of thing every day. Instead, we ended up here, with all these memories tucked away in a cupboard. I know. Sometimes I think about how lucky we were to have those early years. Even though we didn’t have much, we had each other and those toys. They helped us create our own world. And it’s funny, isn’t it? Even now, with all the problems in the world, I think about how simple life was back then.

I swear, the mosquitoes around here are getting worse every summer. I’ve never had such a bad time in the park with the baby. I feel like I’m more of a target than the baby! I know what you mean. I’ve been swatting them all morning. It’s like they’re all out to get us. I think they must have a vendetta against parents with babies. I’m not sure if it’s a vendetta or just the season. It’s just so annoying. I can’t even enjoy the sun without feeling like I’ve been attacked. Yeah, but at least it’s not the traffic. That’s something else I haven’t been able to get used to. Every time we drive to the park, it’s like we’re in a game of chicken with the cars. I know, I know. I was about to say something about the traffic, too. It’s just so frustrating. I was in a hurry this morning, and I almost got stuck behind a van for ten minutes. I can only imagine. I had to get to the music gig last night, and the traffic was a nightmare. I didn’t even make it on time. I was so late, the band had already started playing without me. Oh no, that’s not good. I guess you missed out on the first few songs? Yeah, and I was so upset. I’ve been dying to hear them play live. I think they’re really good. They have a real vibe. It’s like they’re not just playing music, they’re telling a story. That sounds amazing. I’ve been meaning to check them out. I’m not a huge fan of the genre, but I’m curious. Maybe I’ll go to one of their gigs next week. You should. It’s not just about the music—it’s about the energy. You can feel it in the room. It’s like the whole crowd is part of the performance. I’ll consider it. I just need to figure out how to get there without getting stuck in traffic again. I think I’ll take the bus this time. At least then I won’t have to deal with the cars. That sounds like a plan. And maybe I can join you. I really need to experience that energy.

Hey, you’re late. Did you get stuck in traffic or something? No, I just had a lot on my mind. You know how it is—working on applications, trying to figure out where I’m going with my life. It’s been a rough few days. I get it. I’ve been training a lot lately, trying to get into the right shape for the next competition. It’s not just about the skill, it’s about fitness too. You know, the whole package. Yeah, I can imagine. I’ve been trying to keep up with my fitness too, but without a gym, it’s hard. I’ve been doing some home workouts, but I miss the real thing. I could show you some basic exercises. Maybe we could do a few together. It’d be good to get some activity in. It also helps with the mental stuff, you know? That sounds nice. I’d like that. Maybe later this week? Sure, I’ll get back to you. Speaking of which, I saw your post about your job applications. Are you still looking for something? Yep, I’ve sent out a few more applications. It’s been tough, though. I was hoping to get into something at the university, but with the economy the way it is, it’s hard to find anything. It’s not easy for anyone these days. I’ve heard that the job market is pretty tight. But you’re not alone in this. You just have to keep pushing. Thanks. I really appreciate your support. I guess it’s just a matter of time. Definitely. I mean, I was in the same boat a few years ago. I had to work my way up from the ground. Sometimes it takes a while, but it does pay off. I hope so. I’ve got a few interviews coming up. I just have to be ready. Speaking of interviews, did you hear about the new recruitment drive for the golf club? Yeah, I did. They’re looking for people with experience, but I’m not sure if I’m the right fit. Still, it’s worth keeping an eye on. That’s a good idea. Maybe I can help you with your application. You know, I’m not great with the tech stuff, but I can help you with the writing. That’d be great. I’d appreciate that.

So, what’s with the cloud song again? You’ve been singing it non-stop since we got here. It’s not just a song, Dad. It’s a  whole  thing. I got it from a YouTube video. It’s called “Cloudy with a Chance of Meatballs,” and it’s  so  catchy. Yeah, yeah, I’ve heard it. But you’re not going to convince me that a cloud can actually  rain  meatballs. That’s just childish. Oh, come on, it’s a metaphor. It’s a  fantasy . You know how kids are—they live in a world of imagination. And you, Dad, are just sad you missed the era of cartoons with meatball clouds. You’re stuck in the past. I’ll have you know, I  did  watch some of those cartoons. I just don’t like to admit it. Well, maybe I should’ve been more open to the wonders of childhood. Anyway, what are we having for dinner? You said we were going to make something “different.” I was thinking of making a pasta dish. Maybe some carbonara? It’s simple and doesn’t take too long. Carbonara? That sounds amazing. But can I add some extra cheese? Like,  a lot  of cheese? You’re 12, not a toddler. You can have as much cheese as you want. Just don’t make it a  cheese monster . Don’t let him get carried away. I’ll be the one cleaning up. He’s the one who’s going to be eating it. He’s already got a cheese-covered face from the cloud song! You know, I think that’s the first time I’ve seen you laugh like that in a while. You should try being more engaged with the kids. I know. It’s just hard. I’m not used to being around kids all the time. Not since the last one left. You know, he’s kind of cute. And he does sing really well. Maybe we can start a band. A band? You’d be the lead singer, and the toddler would be the backup. That’s the only way it works. I suppose it’s not all bad. Just need to get used to this new life. Yeah, it’s weird, but I like it. It’s like having a new adventure every day. Even if it involves clouds and cheese. Yeah, it’s not perfect, but it’s something.

I swear, I woke up this morning and found ANON still wearing his pants from last night. He said he’d got up and gone to the loo, but somehow he ended up back in bed in them. It’s like he’s trying to make me feel guilty for making him sleep in them in the first place! Oh no, that’s ridiculous. I think he just forgot where he left them. You know how kids are — they’re so forgetful. But I bet he’s going to tell you it was a  statement  or something. You know, like a fashion statement. Yeah, but I saw him earlier. He was sitting on the floor with a clipboard and a pencil, drawing like he’s planning a house extension. He says he’s going to add a new room to the back. A new room? What? Is he building a  fort ? He’s only five, he doesn’t need a new room! No, no, no. He’s got some kind of idea. He says he wants to turn the garage into a playroom, and maybe even build a treehouse up in the garden. He’s got all these crayon sketches and everything. I asked him if he’s been watching  Ferris Bueller’s Day Off , and he just nodded like he’s been dreaming about it all week. That’s not unusual. Kids have wild imaginations. I mean, he’s got a teacher for a parent, so I guess he’s been exposed to all that creative stuff. But honestly, he’s got a point — the house is old, and the garage is really just a glorified shed. Maybe he’s onto something. I think he’s trying to make the house feel more like a place for  us  too. He says he wants to make it a place where we can all run around and have adventures, like a real family home. Well, if that’s what he wants, then maybe we should just give him the run of the place. I mean, I don’t know how we’re going to fit all of us in there if he builds a treehouse and a playroom. Exactly! I think it’s time we start planning the extension properly. I’ll talk to the council about getting planning permission. Maybe we can even get some grant money for it. It could be a big project.

I've been thinking about redecorating my flat in Cairo. It’s been a while since I’ve done anything with the walls. I’m starting to feel like I need a bit of a change after all this time in the same place. That sounds like a good idea. I’ve been meaning to do the same in my place in Cardiff. I actually just picked up some new ideas from a design magazine I found in the university library. Do you have a particular style you’re going for? Honestly, I haven’t decided yet. I like the minimalist style, but I also love some traditional elements. Maybe something that mixes both? It’s tricky, though, because the walls are pretty plain and I don’t want to go overboard. Yeah, mixing styles can be a bit of a challenge, but it can also be very rewarding. I went for a mix of modern and rustic in my living room, and it turned out quite nicely. I actually got some inspiration from a trip I took to Italy a few years back. The architecture there is amazing, isn’t it? Oh, yes! I’d love to visit Italy again. I went a few times in the early days, back when I was still in Cairo. The people, the food, the history—it’s all so rich. I remember one time I was in Florence, and I stumbled upon a small café that had the best espresso I’ve ever had. That’s a great memory. I’ve never been to Italy, but I’ve always wanted to. I was thinking about applying for a research grant to study the water companies in Italy. It’s a bit of an unusual topic, but I think it could be interesting. I’ve been working on a proposal for the academic council. That sounds ambitious. I’ve been working on a similar project—trying to get funding for a research paper on the Hadron collider. It’s hard to get that kind of support, especially with the current budget constraints. I know, it’s tough. But I think if you can show the potential impact, even a small grant can make a big difference. Maybe we can help each other out with the proposals? I’ve got a few ideas on how to frame them better. That would be great. It’s always helpful to have another set of eyes and a different perspective.

I can’t believe it’s already April. You know what that means, lads? Easter chocolate time! Yeah, I love Easter chocolate! Especially the ones with marshmallows. They’re so sweet and sticky. Do we have any this year? I hope so! My mum always buys the big boxes with all the different types. I tried to eat one yesterday, but it was too much. I had to save some for later. Oh, I remember when I was your age. We used to have the same thing. Didn’t your mum always say, “Save some for the adults”? It was mostly just a way to get us to stop eating too much! She still says that. I don’t know why. I’m not a kid anymore! Yeah, but I still think it’s funny. I mean, it’s not like we’re adults. We’re just kids who like chocolate. Maybe she’s just being dramatic. You know, I was thinking earlier about the renovations at Granny’s. I was going to suggest we do some work on the living room. Maybe we can make a new space for the Lego collection. That sounds great! I’ve been collecting so much Lego lately. I got a whole set of the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles last week. It’s so cool. I’m trying to build the whole city. I have one too! I’m working on the Shredder’s lair. It’s taking me forever. I even have to sort out all the pieces because I mix them up. Oh, I know that feeling. I used to do that when I was about your age. Maybe we should all gather the Lego and sort it out together. It might be fun. Maybe we can even make a new display. That would be so cool! I could show off my stuff. And maybe we can all play with it at the same time. It’d be like a Lego party! Yeah! I could even bring out my Harry Potter set. I’ve been building the Hogwarts castle with my brother. It’s almost done. That sounds like a plan. I’ll make some cocoa and we can set up the room. It’ll be like our own mini cinema. We could even watch The Simpsons or Harry Potter on the projector. I can’t wait! I think I’ll get my special chocolate and bring it in.

I can’t believe it’s been a month since I came back from that holiday. Time flies, doesn’t it? I know, I’m still getting used to being back. I missed you so much, but I also missed my routine. I kind of got used to not having to make my own meals all the time. Yeah, I know what you mean. I actually tried cooking a few meals while I was away, but honestly, I just ended up eating out more. It’s not like I had a chef in the villa, and I didn’t want to mess with the kitchen. That sounds frustrating. I made sure to plan a few meals, but honestly, I found myself needing a break from cooking too. I even tried some of those meal kits from the shop. It was kind of fun, but not quite the same as cooking from scratch. I’d love to try that. I’ve been thinking about doing some cooking classes in the new year, maybe with a friend or two. Do you want to come? It might be a good way to meet people and get some new skills. I’d like that. I’ve been meaning to get back into cooking, and maybe it would be a good chance to work on my confidence in the kitchen. Though I’m still nervous about burning the toast, honestly. Oh, come on! We all have that moment. I burned a whole plate of pancakes once. It was a disaster. I just kept saying, “It’s just toast!” But it was a mess. That’s the worst! I once tried making a soufflé and it collapsed like a house of cards. I ended up eating it with a spoon. It was so sad. I remember when I tried to make my first soufflé. I followed the recipe to the letter, and it still collapsed. My flatmate thought I was trying to play a prank on them. They just kept staring at the plate like it was alien life. That’s so funny. I could see that happening. I think I’ll stick to simple meals for now. Unless we try that cooking class—maybe I’ll be ready by then. Perfect. I’ll start looking into classes. And maybe I’ll bring some snacks or something to share. I made these really good homemade biscuits that I brought back from the trip.

Right, I’ve got everything we need for the week, but let me check again. We’ve got the basics—bread, milk, eggs, and the usual veggies. But I’m wondering, have you thought about what you’d like for dinner this weekend?      Honestly, I was just thinking about that! My mates and I are going to a new place in York this Saturday. It’s a place that serves really good fish and chips, and they’ve got a live band playing. I thought maybe we could all go together.      Sounds like a plan, but I’m not sure if I’ll make it. I’ve been feeling a bit under the weather lately. The doctor said I need to take it easy.      That’s understandable, dear. You’ve been working too hard. I remember when I was younger, I used to drive all over the county, but now I’m just content with a cup of tea and a bit of knitting.      Well, if you can’t make it, we can still have a quiet evening at home. I’ve been thinking of making some proper Yorkshire pudding and roast beef. It’s been too long since we had that kind of meal.      That sounds brilliant! I can help you with the cooking. I’ve been practicing my roasting skills in the kitchen at home. Though I’m not sure my mum would approve of me using a meat thermometer—she still thinks it’s a science experiment.      Oh, you know your mum. She’s always been the same. But I still remember when I used to cook for the family. Back in the day, we barely had time to sit down, let alone cook. My kids would have been running around the house like headless chickens.      And you know what they say about mothers—their children never understand them. But I think you did a great job. Even though I never got to see much of you, I always knew you were hardworking.      That’s the spirit. Anyway, let’s get back to the groceries. If we’re going to have a roast this weekend, we need to make sure we have enough potatoes and carrots. And maybe some Yorkshire sauce, just in case.      I’ll grab the potatoes. I’ve got a whole bag from the market. And I think I can still find a tin of sauce if I look hard enough.

I just watched  Peter Pan  again with the kids, and it reminded me of how much I loved that film when I was younger. It’s such a magical story, isn’t it? Yeah, it’s amazing! I love how the characters are so full of life. But wait, isn’t there another version of  Peter Pan  that’s more recent? I think it's called  Pan ? I think that's the one! I remember seeing it with my dad. It’s supposed to be a darker version, right? Not as happy as the original. Oh, I’ve heard about that! It made me a bit nervous when I first heard about it. I wasn’t sure if it would be too scary for the kids. But I guess it’s good to show them different versions of the same story. But isn’t  Peter Pan  based on a book? I think the original story is by J.M. Barrie, right? Yes, exactly! The story first appeared in a play, and then it was adapted into books and films. I remember reading the original version when I was in secondary school. It was different from the Disney version, though. There were more complex themes, like loss and growing up. Does that mean  Pan  is based on the same book? No, actually,  Pan  is more like a reimagining. It’s set in the 1980s and follows a boy named Peter who is adopted by a man named Jack, who is a pirate. It’s a very different take on the story, and it’s supposed to be more realistic. That sounds interesting. I wonder why they made such a different version. I think it was an attempt to give the story a more mature perspective. But it didn’t do well at the box office. Some people found it too dark or confusing. I think my grandpa said it was too scary for kids. He said he didn’t like the way the characters were portrayed. That’s true. The original  Peter Pan  is more about imagination and the idea of never growing up, which is a theme that’s still very popular today. I think that's why it continues to be beloved by so many people. I love that idea. It’s like a dream that never fades. Maybe that’s why we all still love the story, even as we grow older.

So, we've got about 45 minutes before we get to the airport, and I think we're going to be stuck in traffic again. It's always like this in the mornings, isn't it? I swear, the roads in Devon have gotten worse since we moved here.      I know, I know. It’s ridiculous. I think it’s because more people are working from home now, but still, they all have to commute at the same time. I’ve had to leave the house at 6:30 just to get to the school by 8:15. I barely have time to even make my coffee.      Well, at least you don’t have to deal with the same kind of commute I do. I still live in Taunton, and it’s a 40-minute drive just to get to work, and that’s if there’s no traffic. I’ve been thinking about moving closer to the city, but the cost of housing is just too high, even for someone with a graduate degree.      You know, I had a similar thought when I was working in management. I used to live in Exeter, and it only took me 20 minutes to get to work, then again, I had a car and a decent salary. These days, I’m barely getting out of bed by 8, and I’m still not sure if I’ll even make it to the airport on time.      I hear you. I’ve been trying to adjust my routine, but it’s not easy. I’d rather have a 45-minute commute than be stuck in a house with no balcony or garden. I’ve been dreaming about buying a place in the countryside, just something with a bit more space and peace.      I’d love that. I’ve always wanted to have a house with a garden, even if it’s just a small one. My parents used to have a place in Cornwall, and I remember how peaceful it was there. I can still see the sea from my bedroom window. I’m going to try and plan a family trip there for Christmas.      That sounds lovely. I’ve got my sister coming over for the holidays, and she’s always wanted to visit Cornwall. If we can manage the driving, we’ll go. I’ve also been thinking about hosting a house-warming party for my new flat.

I've been meaning to ask you, what do you think about the Swedish massage? I read somewhere it's supposed to be really beneficial for stress relief. Oh, I've had one before, actually. It's quite different from the regular massages I've had. The pressure is more focused, and it's supposed to help with muscle tension. But I must say, I was a bit nervous at first, thinking it might be too intense. I can imagine. I've never tried it, but I've heard a lot about the benefits. It's interesting how different types of massage can have such varied effects. I mean, even the terminology—like Swedish, deep tissue, or shiatsu—can be confusing at first. Definitely. I think it's all about understanding what works for you. I suppose it's one of those things where you just have to give it a go. Speaking of which, I heard there's going to be a big event for the ME next year, and they're really pushing for more female involvement. Have you heard anything about that? Yes, I have. It's quite a significant event, I think. They’re trying to bring more women into leadership roles and highlight their contributions. It's a bit of a shift in the way things have been done before. I remember when I was younger, women were often overlooked in these kinds of discussions. You're right. It’s a shame it took so long for that to happen. I suppose change doesn’t come easily. But I do think it's a positive step forward. I wonder how it'll affect the future of these events and the way they're organized. I can only hope it makes a tangible difference. It's frustrating to see the same old faces at these events, isn't it? I think it's important to bring new perspectives and new voices into the conversation. Absolutely. And I've been thinking about my wife lately. She's been talking about retiring early and maybe going back to work part-time. I've been helping her look into nursery education options. It's a bit of a puzzle, but I suppose it's part of life. That sounds like a big decision. I know how difficult it can be to balance work and family. But I think it's about finding the right fit for everyone involved.

I just got the email from the travel agency about the holiday in Spain. They said the dates are confirmed, and the villa is all set. I’m really excited, aren’t you? Yes, I am, love. It’s been so long since we’ve had a proper holiday together. I remember when we first went to the Costa del Sol, back in the late 90s. You were still teaching English in Manchester, and I was working as a social worker in Cardiff. What a different time. It feels like a lifetime ago. I can’t believe how much has changed. I’ve been teaching for over ten years now, and I still love it. It’s just nice to have a break and not have to worry about lesson plans for a week. I know, I know. It’s a good idea to take a little time for yourself, especially after all that work. You’re doing such a great job teaching, but you deserve some rest. Spain sounds perfect. The weather is always warm, and the food is amazing. I was thinking about that too. I’ve always loved the Mediterranean. I might take some cooking classes while we’re there. I’ve been wanting to improve my Spanish, and maybe even try my hand at making paella. That sounds like a wonderful idea. I could help you with the recipes, and maybe we can join a local tour group. It’s always better to travel with someone you know and trust, isn’t it? Absolutely. I was also thinking about the kids. We should make sure they have a good time too. Maybe we can take them to the beach every day and let them run around. It’ll be so nice to see them laughing and playing without the usual schedule. That’s what I was hoping for too. I know they’ve been so busy with school and extracurricular activities. A little time off will do them good. I’ve even started packing some of their clothes. It’s not too late to adjust the list if you need. That’s really thoughtful of you. I’ll take a look at the packing list tonight. I’m just so grateful we’re doing this. It’s been a while since we’ve truly connected like this. I know, love. It’s not just about the holiday—it’s about being together, reminiscing, and looking forward to the future.

Hey, mate, you've been really quiet lately. Everything okay? I noticed you've been checking your phone a lot, and I saw some messages about a recent transaction. What's going on? Oh, yeah, sorry about that. I’ve been dealing with some stuff at work. You know how it is—some projects come with a lot of back-and-forth. But I’m fine, don’t worry. A few transactions here and there, nothing too big. Right, I heard you were managing a few accounts. I mean, that’s a big deal. You’ve always been good with numbers, but juggling multiple things—sounds intense. How’s the team handling it? It’s a bit of a rollercoaster, honestly. But I’ve got a solid team, and I’m pretty confident in my skills. I mean, I did get a promotion last year, so it’s all part of the climb. Just trying to stay on top of it. That’s great, man. I’m so proud of you. You’ve worked so hard for it. I remember when we were in school, I used to struggle with math, and you were like the textbook. Now you’re a manager? That’s insane. Nah, don’t get too ahead of yourself. I’m still learning. And it’s not all smooth sailing. I’ve had my share of ups and downs, but I’m getting better at handling the pressure. Speaking of pressure, how’s your uni work going? I heard you’re in your final year. Yeah, I’m wrapping things up. It’s been a wild ride, but I’m ready to take a break. I’ve been thinking about what I want to do next. Maybe something related to sports? I’ve been into cricket lately, and I’m trying to get into it more seriously. That’s cool. You’ve always had a passion for sport. I remember when we used to play in the park as kids. Do you think you’ll be playing professionally or just doing it for fun? I’m not sure yet. I’m thinking about coaching or maybe writing about sports. I’ve been following a few celebrities in the field, like that new cricket commentator—his insight is so sharp. It’s inspiring. Yeah, he’s a good guy. I’ve seen a few of his interviews. You might want to check him out.

Hello? Oh, it’s me, Bob. Sorry to bother you, but I’ve got this terrible pain in my leg again. It’s been bothering me all day. Oh, Bob, don’t worry, I’m just having a cup of tea and listening to the radio. Is it the same old leg? Mmm, I heard the phone ring. Is everything alright, Bob? Yeah, just the usual. It’s been a bit of a nightmare. I was trying to make a cuppa, and I slipped on the stairs. Oh no! You must have hurt yourself. Are you okay? I think I’ve sprained it, but it’s not too bad. I’m just waiting for it to settle. I’ve been meaning to talk to you about this old globe you had in your shed, you know, the one from the 60s. It’s got all the countries, and it’s got a bit of a crack in it, but it’s still pretty good. Oh, Bob, I remember that globe. It was one of those ones you could spin around, and you could really get a feel for the world. I used to love it when we were kids. I think it might have been your dad’s. Yeah, my mum had one just like it. I remember she used to point out places when we were on holiday. We went to Yorkshire once, and she showed us all the hills and dales. Yorkshire! That’s where I used to go on holiday with my mates. We stayed in youth hostels and slept on the floor. It was the best kind of holiday. I remember that. You used to say you could sleep anywhere as long as there was a bed. I always thought you were a bit mad, but I suppose it’s the youth hostel spirit. Yeah, it’s funny how those things stay with you. I think the best part was the people you met. You never knew who you’d meet in a youth hostel. Exactly. You could be talking to someone from London one minute and someone from the north the next. It was like a bit of the world in one place. It’s funny how the old places and the old ways still feel so close, even when you’re not there. Yeah, and the underground system in London was the same. It felt like you could go anywhere in the world, but it was just a few stops away.

Right, I’ve just checked the flights. The one from Doncaster to Manchester is cheaper, but it’s a bit of a journey. I could do with a bit of time to myself before the trip. Do you think we should take the bus instead? Wait, we’re going to Manchester? I thought we were going to Leeds. Oh, you’ve changed your mind. That’s fine, I guess. But don’t you think the bus is going to be a nightmare? I’ve heard the roads are a bit of a mess after dark. I know, I know. But I figured we could do the drive together and save money on accommodation. Plus, I’ve got a bit of a layover in Manchester, so I can explore the city a bit before the actual conference. It’ll be a nice change of scenery. Yeah, I get that. But what’s the deal with the conference, anyway? You’ve been talking about it for weeks. Is it really that important? I mean, it’s a big opportunity. It’s the biggest event of the year in the industry, and I’ve got a presentation to do. Right, so, do you know what you're doing next week? I got the shift sorted at the pub, but I’m still trying to figure out how to juggle that with my postgrad stuff. Honestly, I’m still not sure. I've been meaning to ask, how’s your holiday going, Sarah? I know you said you were going to the Scottish Highlands. Oh, it’s been lovely, thank you. The scenery there is just breathtaking. I can't believe the amount of fast food we've eaten this week. I know it's just a week, but I feel like I'm starting to develop a taste for it. It's not just you. I've been thinking about the same thing. It's been so much easier than cooking, and besides, when you're watching the Euros, you just want to eat something quick and easy. I know, but I feel guilty about it. I mean, I used to cook all the time back in Sunderland. Even though I lived alone, I always made sure to have a proper meal. Now, with all the football matches and everything, I just end up grabbing a burger or something. My mum used to say that you can tell a lot about someone's life by the way they eat. She always thought that people who ate fast food were lazy or just didn't care about their health. I guess she was right in a way. But I think in our case, it's more about convenience than anything else. I suppose. I mean, I do try to cook more often, but when I'm not in the mood, or when it's late and I'm tired, it's just too tempting. I mean, how many times have I seen people just grabbing a bite at the local chip shop while watching a match? Oh, I know. I think it's part of the culture now. If you're watching the Euros, it's almost expected. Like, someone has to bring the chips, someone else brings the crisps, and we just eat them all while talking about the game. It's almost like a tradition. Yeah, it’s like a ritual. I remember when I was in Birmingham, the pubs always had this sort of vibes during a big match. People would just sit and enjoy the game and the food. It's something that brings people together, even if it's just eating chips and beer. Exactly. And the football is a great excuse to eat. I don't think I've ever been more motivated to eat than when there's a match on. Even if it's just a random game on the telly, I feel like I need to be part of the experience. That's true. It really does make life more enjoyable.

Mum, I was just thinking — have you seen the new film coming out? The one with that actor from  Inception ? It’s got a bit of a British accent, which I found interesting. Oh, you mean  Deer Hunter ? But I’ll be thinking about this conversation all day. It’s amazing how movies can bring people together, isn’t it? Well, that’s the beauty of them, isn’t it? They remind us of where we’ve been and who we were. I’m just glad we’ve got a few more years left to enjoy them.

So, I just had a conversation with the children about Pancake Day. You know, the one where they eat pancakes and throw them at each other? Well, they think it’s a  big  deal.      Yeah, I was in the kitchen when they were arguing about who got the last pancake. They were basically throwing them at each other like it’s a competition.      And then they were all talking about the school assembly. They said the head teacher told them about the Science Museum trip. They’re super excited about it.      Of course they are. Well, they’re not exactly  allowed  to bring a tent, but I guess they’re just being adventurous.      Speaking of adventures, did you hear about the Festival Hall events? They’re only kids. They’ll be fine.      Yeah, but we should make sure they’re washing their hands too. It’s important.      True. But before that, let’s make sure they actually eat their food. I’ve seen them throw things out.      That’s our kids. They’re growing up, and they’ve got their own opinions.      Yeah, and they’re going to Paris next year.

So, I was just thinking about the old days when we used to go to the market every Saturday. Remember when we used to argue over whether the rice krispy cakes were worth the price? It was a battle every time.      Oh, you were always the one who was too particular about the texture. I remember once you got so upset that the shopkeeper thought you were trying to sabotage the product.      That was a classic! And don’t even get me started on the Scan As You Go systems in the supermarkets now. I still can’t get used to paying at the end of the aisle.      I know, right? I still feel like I’m about to be caught shoplifting if I don’t keep my hands in sight. But I suppose it’s just the way things are now.      It’s all about convenience, I suppose. I still remember when we had to carry all those bags home in the old days, and the milk would go bad if you weren’t quick enough.      I think I still have the old grocery list in my drawer. I wrote it down in a different way—more like a recipe, with notes on how much to buy for the week.      That must be the one with the “charming” comment about the store’s manager. I remember that. He used to laugh when you wrote that.      Oh yes, he was a character. He said he’d never forget the day you told him he had the personality of a cow.      And he didn’t. He repeated it at every staff meeting for years.      I think we all have those stories from the past. It’s funny how they stick with you. Speaking of old days, I was thinking about the time you tried to teach me how to drive.      Oh, that was a disaster. I was trying to show you how to parallel park, and the moment I tried to reverse, you veered straight into the hedge.      And you were trying to be the cool instructor, with your hands on the wheel, no hands on the wheel—wait, what was that?      I think it was more of a drift than a reverse. I remember the look on your face when we pulled up in the driveway with the car completely upside down.      You had the courage of a lion and the precision of a blindfolded man.

I just got a new recipe for dumplings from a friend, and I thought we could try it for Chinese New Year. It’s supposed to be really tasty, and it’s got a few ingredients we might have at home. Can we have meat in them? I like meat dumplings. I like vegetables. I think they’re healthier. I know, they have a vegetarian option too. Especially since we're celebrating Chinese New Year, and it's one of the traditional dishes. I heard you were going to draw a dragon for the festival. Is that going to be fun? I remember when I was a kid, I used to draw ones with wings and everything. I like to draw stars and planets. I did a whole picture of the solar system last week. That’s great! Maybe after the dragon drawing, we could talk about it more. It’s a great way to stay active and creative. And I want to play the drums. I think it’s like the drum lessons I heard about.

So, do you think we should go to the Pantheon tonight? I’ve heard it’s beautiful at night. I’m with you on that. But I was thinking, maybe we could grab a bite first? I’m actually running a café in Birmingham, but I’ve been thinking about doing a little trip to Rome for a while. It’s interesting how different the atmosphere is here compared to the UK. You should definitely go. I’ve got a cousin in Florence, and if you need a place to stay, I can help. Just let me know. And don’t forget to try the gelato—it’s world-class.

So, I've been feeling really off for the past couple of days, like I’ve got a cold or something. I thought I was just tired from work, but now I’m sure it’s something more. So, I've been thinking about our shopping list. I think we need to get some fresh fruit and veggies, and maybe some bread. Oh, and don’t forget the birthday cards for the kids. So, I've been thinking about the heating system in this old place. It's been a bit temperamental, and I don't know if I should just replace it or try to fix what's there. I’ve had some experience with heating systems from my teaching days—though I mostly dealt with the classroom, not the underfloor ones. But I know a few plumbers who do renovations. I just finished my meal, and I’m still thinking about how much I miss the days when I could just grab a sandwich and go. These long afternoons at the lab, with all the paperwork and data entry, it’s easy to feel like I’ve lost touch with the simpler things. I know what you mean. I used to be the same way. I think the more we take care of ourselves, the better we’ll be at everything else. And honestly, I think it’s something our kids are going to respect more than anything else.

So, I was just telling my sister about the cat that ran into the garden and got stuck in the hedge. It was  so  dramatic. I mean, it was just a little orange tabby, but it looked like it was about to give up.      Sounds like the same one that used to knock over the vase every time it heard the microwave. I remember one time it nearly got stuck in the oven, too. You think it was trying to get to the chicken?      That’s the one! I swear it had a personality. I used to call it Mr. Whiskers, but only when I was alone. It would stare at me like it knew I was lying. And you know what? It was the only one who ever showed up when I was late for work. It’d just sit there and wait.      I had a dog like that. Named Bingo, and it was a real drama queen. Once it ran off and got stuck in a drainpipe for over an hour. I had to climb up and get it down. Felt like a superhero, but it only took me five minutes. Still, I didn’t get a medal.      I’m sorry to say, I’ve never had a pet. I’ve tried, but my mum always says I’m allergic. She’s right, too. I sneeze just looking at them. Though, I do love the way cats can just walk into your lap and start purring like a little engine. It’s so calming.      Yeah, there’s something about their purring. It’s like they’re singing to you. I’ve had a few cats in my life, and they always seem to know when you’re upset. Even the one that knocked over the vase. It’d come and rub against my leg when I was crying.      I think they’re just trying to get your attention. Maybe they’re saying, “Hey, you’ve got a mess here. Do something about it.”      Or maybe they’re just saying, “You’re the boss, so go fix it.” It’s like they’re working for you.      I think they’re just trying to get your food. Every time I have a snack, they’re there like, “Whoa, that’s mine.”      Sounds like they’re not too bad. I mean, they’re kind of like little roommates. They’re there, they’re messy, but they’re also kind of cute.

So, I've been thinking about going to the coast for a bit of a break. Maybe somewhere like Scarborough or Whitby? I could do with a change of scenery, you know?      Aye, I’ve been there a few times. Used to go with my lass when we were younger. The place is full of history, and the views are just stunning. You should go.      That sounds like a great idea. I’ve been meaning to visit the North East myself. I was born in Hertfordshire, but I’ve always been fascinated by the northern part of England. I mean, I’ve been to Manchester and Liverpool, but not really the coastal areas.      I know what you mean. I’ve never gone far from Sunderland, but I’d love to explore more. I’ve heard the coast is beautiful, and the food there must be amazing.      Oh, you don’t know the half of it. The fish and chips there are to die for. My wife and I love to cook, but I think it’s important to try local specialties sometimes. Have you ever been to a traditional pub in the North?      I have, actually. I went to a place in Newcastle a few years ago. The atmosphere was so lively, and the ale was top-notch. I think I’ll be going back there soon.      That’s good. I’ve always said that the North has the best pubs. It’s a real community thing. You know, people are more friendly up there. You can talk to anyone, and they’ll give you the time of day.      That’s true. I’ve always found people in the North to be very welcoming. I think it’s part of the culture. I remember when I first moved to Manchester, I was a bit nervous, but everyone was so friendly.      That’s amazing. I suppose it’s all about the people. I’ve never really had that experience in the South. I mean, I’ve been to London, but it’s a different vibe.      Aye, I get that. London’s a different kettle of fish. It’s always busy, and people are on the go. But there’s something special about the North.

I can't believe we've got to this point already. It's been ages since we last planned a class together. What's been going on with you? Honestly, I’ve been trying to figure out what to teach next. I can't believe we've got to this point. That coffee machine we bought last year is still going, and yet we’re already thinking about replacing it. It’s not even broken, just… old. I know, I know, but the truth is, it’s been a pain in the neck ever since we moved here. The one in Dublin was much better. I miss that one. Yeah, but we can’t keep putting it off. You know how much it costs to get it fixed now. And with the removal and storage costs for the old house, it’s just not worth it. I’m not sure, though. It feels like we’ve been running on fumes since we moved. I’ve been thinking about how much easier it would be if we could just take a step back and not have to worry about all this. I agree, but maybe we need to plan properly. I mean, we’re not as young as we used to be, and I don’t want to be scrambling at the last minute. True, but I’m still trying to wrap my head around the politics of it all. I mean, the Labour leadership—what’s going on with that? I can’t even follow it anymore. I know. It’s all so confusing. I tried to watch one of their debates the other day, and I just couldn’t get into it. I mean, I used to be all about idealism, but now I just want stability. That’s the thing, isn’t it? When you grow up in an environment like mine, you’re taught to believe in something bigger. But now, with everything that’s happening, I’m not sure what that even means anymore. I know what you mean. I used to be so idealistic too. I used to think that changing the world was just a matter of trying hard enough. But now, with all the things we’ve gone through, I’m not sure I believe that anymore. It’s tough, isn’t it? I think we all have to find our own way through this. Maybe we just need to focus on the things we can control—for now.

So, I've been meaning to ask—what's with the name  ANON ANON ? It’s like a username or something.      Oh, it’s a pseudonym we picked for the trip. We didn’t want to use our real names in case someone recognized us. Plus, it’s kind of funny.      I get it. It’s like a nickname for a group. Though I still can’t figure out why you used  ANON  twice.      It’s a bit of a joke. Like, “Anon, Anon, we’re just regular people.” It’s got a bit of a  Harry Potter  vibe, honestly.      Haha, I like it. It’s catchy and mysterious. But I was thinking—do you guys ever get tired of using pseudonyms? Like, aren’t we just people with real names?      Honestly, sometimes. But it’s fun, you know? Like a game. Plus, it helps keep things light when we’re out and about.      I get it. But I still think we should start calling each other by our real names. I mean, it’s not like we’re in a cult or anything.      Yeah, but if we do that, what do we call ourselves?  Baker’s Noodle ,  Café Chica , and  Microwave Prince ? That’s too much.      Wait, where did  Microwave Prince  come from?      From the  microwave  we used to heat up our food. I’m not proud of it, but it’s a thing.      I think that’s the highlight of our trip—the  microwave . It’s like the only thing that worked in that restaurant.      Seriously, the microwave was a lifeline. I mean, I tried using the oven, but it was too hot, and the  condiments  were out of order.      Condiments? What condiments?      You know—ketchup, mayonnaise, mustard. The place had none of it. I had to ask the waiter, and he said they only had  Italian  stuff.      Wait,  Italian ? Like  salsa ?      No, like  oli  or something. I asked, and he said it was  kosher .      Oh,  kosher ! That explains a lot. I thought it was just a fancy way of saying “no onions.”      Was it?      No, it was  kosher law . We tried to order a  club sandwich  and the chef said it wasn’t allowed. It was super weird.      Yeah, and if you look at the  canal boats  they’ve got up there, they’ve got their own  river names . I’m not sure if it’s a sign or a warning.

Alright, so I just got back from my weekend trip to Manchester. I met this guy on Tinder, and he was  so  into me. We ended up going out for a drink, and he even asked me to his place. Not sure if I should take it further or just keep things casual. Oh no,  again ? I thought you were over that phase. You’ve been matching with guys on Tinder like it’s your job. What’s the deal, are you trying to find a partner or just passing time? I don’t know, it’s just the uni life. Everyone’s like, “You’ve got to find someone, you’re not getting any younger.” But honestly, I’m just trying to enjoy my time without too much pressure. Yeah, I hear you. I’m not even on Tinder anymore. I’m just focused on uni and my housemates. It’s weird, though—my flatmates are all like, “You’ve got to meet someone, it’s not fair you’re still single.” But I’m not ready for that kind of pressure. I can totally relate. My housemates are always going on about their boyfriends and how they’re “so lucky.” It’s like, I’m not even in a relationship, and they’re pretending they know what I’m going through. It’s kinda annoying. Yeah, but don’t get me wrong—I  do  want to find someone. It’s just, I don’t want someone who’s just looking for a quick fling or a steady partner. I want someone who’s compatible and actually wants a real relationship. I get that. I think it’s just about knowing what you want. I’ve been trying to figure out what I’m looking for too. I mean, Tinder is kind of a mess, but I think the main issue is that people are just looking for validation. It’s not about finding someone, it’s about feeling seen. Exactly. And I think that’s why it’s so hard to find someone who’s genuine. We’re all just looking for that one person who gets us, you know? But sometimes, it feels like the wrong person ends up in the wrong place. I think the key is to go slow. I mean, if you’re not ready for a relationship, don’t force it. Just enjoy being single for a while.

I just watched that new TV show last night. It was about benefits and the government. Felt like it was all pointing fingers at people like us. I mean, it's not like we've done anything wrong, are we? No, I agree. It's just that the media keeps painting us as lazy and taking advantage of the system. I think they just want to make us feel guilty for not working. Exactly. I saw a documentary the other day about how people on benefits are actually contributing to the economy in different ways. They do volunteer work, take care of kids, or help out in the community. It's not just about money. That’s true, but I still feel like the government doesn’t understand that. I mean, I was a civil engineer, and I know what it takes to work. I just can't find anything that suits me now. The economy is so different now, isn’t it? Oh, it’s not just you. Everyone is struggling. I used to run a small business, but it went under. The cost of living has gone up so much, and the support doesn’t keep up with it. I know, and it's so frustrating. I was a childminder for years, and I really enjoyed it. But now, with all the regulations, and the pressure to get back into the workforce, it's hard to stay in what you love. I don’t know what we’re supposed to do. I’ve been looking for work for ages, but everything seems to be going to younger people with more qualifications. I have a graduate degree, and it’s not even considered anymore. I think we’re just being left behind. The system doesn’t seem to cater to people like us. I’ve been on benefits for years, and I barely make ends meet. It's not enough to pay for even the basics like food and heating. And with the way politics is going, it feels like we’re not even being listened to. I remember when we were getting more support. It’s as if they just want to cut costs without thinking about people’s lives. I suppose the only thing we can do is try to support each other. Maybe get together more, talk about what we want, and see if we can find some way to help one another out.

I can't believe it's already 7pm. I’ve been dicing up the veggies for the stir-fry, and I’m just about to fire up the wok. You’re sure you don’t want to help, love? It’s not like you’ve got anything better to do. I’m just getting out of the office, you know. So, I just looked at my social media feed again. There's this photo of my old flat in Cambridge, and I thought, “God, I haven’t been there in years.”      That’s the thing, isn’t it? Sometimes you look at a photo and it feels like you’re still there, even if you’ve never really been back.      Exactly. I mean, I was supposed to go back for my dad’s funeral, but I couldn’t get the money together. It was like the timing just never worked out.      I know how that feels. I still can’t go back to Bury, not since the job changed. It’s not like I’m avoiding it, though. I just feel like I’m not part of that place anymore.      You know, I was thinking the other day about what I would do if I had to work again. I’d probably end up being a teacher again, like you, even if it’s part-time. It’s just the only thing I’ve ever been any good at.      You don’t have to do that. I mean, you’ve got the qualifications, and you’ve got that extra time. Maybe you could take it slow, like I did. I’m trying to figure out if I want to stay in Poland or go back.      It’s funny, isn’t it? I never thought I’d be someone who would even think about moving. I always assumed I’d just stay in England. Now I’m here, and it’s like I’m looking at things differently.      That makes sense. I mean, you’ve been unemployed for so long, you start to question everything. I’ve been thinking about therapy too. Not that I need it, but just to clear my head.      I should probably do that too. I’ve been feeling pretty down lately. It’s not that I’m sad, it’s just... I don’t know. Like I’m stuck in this loop.      I get that. Sometimes you just need someone to talk to. Even if it’s not a professional, like a friend.      Yeah, you’re right. Maybe I should try to get back in touch with some of the old friends I lost touch with. It’s weird, isn’t it? The way people change, and the way places change.      Absolutely. And it’s not just places—sometimes it’s the sense of belonging that shifts.

So, do you know where we can get a decent meal around here? I’m starved, and I don’t fancy another pub dish. Honestly, I’ve been meaning to try that new café on Charing Cross Road. They’ve got this really good vegetarian burger, and the coffee’s amazing. I saw someone from my course eating there last week. Oh, that sounds nice. I’ve been meaning to check it out too. I’ve got a feeling the food’s going to be worth the wait. But you know, I still can’t believe we’re out here drinking tea at 7 PM like it’s the 1960s. Yeah, I know, it’s kinda weird, isn’t it? I mean, I’m a student, so I’m used to café culture, but I still find it funny how people from my family – like my mum and dad – still stick to tea and scones every afternoon like it’s a ritual. It’s a bit of a tradition for them, isn’t it? I remember when I was younger, we’d all gather in the garden for afternoon tea every Sunday. It was like a family event. But now, with everyone so busy, it’s kind of gone. Although, I do miss it. I get that. I think part of it is the pace of life. I mean, I’m working part-time as a survey programmer, and my friends are all in different places – some in London, some in Manchester, some even abroad. It’s a bit hard to keep up with the old habits. Yeah, I can relate. I’m a copywriter, so I work from home a lot. I’m lucky in a way, but it can be lonely sometimes. I think I’ve been trying to make more of an effort to meet up with friends, even if it’s just for a cup of tea and some chat. That’s a good approach. I think it’s easy to get caught up in work and studies, but staying in touch with your roots – or your friends – is important. Also, I always find that eating out with friends makes the work stress easier to forget. Exactly. So, are you up for trying that café tomorrow? I’ll bring my notebook and we can sketch out some ideas for a new campaign, and maybe even test out the burger.

I can’t believe I was woken up at 6:30 this morning. Someone must’ve been up for a snack or something. Did you two get up at all? No, I was still asleep. I only woke up when I heard the toaster go off. It was so loud, I thought someone was yelling! Yeah, I was dreaming about dinosaurs. Then I heard the toaster and I just jumped up. I saw a video of someone doing it and it looked really fun, even though it looked a bit scary. That sounds amazing. I’m going to sign you both up, just so you can have a proper day out. Now, let’s finish our breakfast and get ready for the day. I’ve got some plans for the circus skills course too. Are you going to join us? Yes, I’m going to go with you both. It’s a chance to spend time together and try something new. Alright, let’s get moving. We don’t want to miss the bus.

I just can’t believe how different the political views are between the South and the North. It’s like two entirely different countries, sometimes. It’s not just politics, it’s culture, history, and even accents. I grew up in Wales, and I still feel like we’re treated as second-class citizens in the UK, especially when it comes to Brexit and the economy. Yeah, I’ve noticed that too. Like, in Aberystwyth, people are more progressive, but in some parts of the North, there’s still a strong sense of working-class identity that’s almost conservative. That’s true, but I also think it’s about the people who are in power. You know, the policymakers are mostly from London or the South East. It’s hard for voices from the North or Wales to be heard. Exactly. I remember in my lectures, we’d discuss how post-war policies really shaped the divide. The North was hit hard by deindustrialization, and Wales was left out of the European Union benefits. It’s like we were never given the same opportunities. I’ve heard stories about that. My gran said that when the coal mines closed in her village, people were left with nothing. They had to move south for work, and that changed everything for the family. It’s amazing how much history is still alive in people’s stories. I’ve been through Cornwall, and I can see the contrast with the way people live here. They’re more laid-back, more outdoorsy. It’s a different rhythm of life. Yeah, and it’s not just geography. It’s about identity. I think that’s why there’s so much about Brexit—people feel like their identity is being threatened. It’s not just about the EU, it’s about being seen as part of the UK. Maybe that’s why I’m so interested in politics. I want to make sure my voice is heard, even if I’m just a student. I think it’s important to understand where you come from and how it shapes the way you look at the world. That’s a great attitude. I think that’s why we’re still close, you know? You come from Wales, I’m from London, but we both have that sense of history and identity. It makes our conversations interesting. And it makes us more aware of the divides.

Okay, so I was thinking about the stories we're creating for the Linton Book Festival. I wanted to get your opinions on the next chapter. It's about a character named Helen Moss, right?      Yeah, I like the idea of Helen Moss. She’s so mysterious. I want to know more about her past. Do you think she has any secrets?      I think she might have. Maybe she’s hiding something from the town. Like, maybe she’s not really from around here?      That’s a good point. I was thinking of making her a bit of a ghostly figure. She appears in the village, but no one can catch her. It adds a supernatural element to the story.      I love that idea! It makes the story more magical. But I want to make sure the town is described in a way that feels real. Maybe include some local landmarks?      Like the old mill? I remember we used to go there when we were kids. It’s got that creepy vibe. Maybe Helen Moss is tied to it somehow?      Exactly! I was thinking she might have lived there once. Maybe she was a farmer or something. But something happened, and now she’s stuck between the world of the living and the dead.      That’s really interesting. It makes me think of the stories my grandmother used to tell me about the hills around here. She said there were spirits in the woods.      I’ve heard that too. My dad used to say the woods were full of stories. Maybe Helen Moss is part of that tradition?      I think that’s a great angle. It connects the story to the place and gives it a sense of history. The Linton Book Festival is a perfect platform for this. The audience would love a local story with a twist.      I’m excited to see how the festival will react. I think it’s important to keep the stories rooted in our community. We should make sure to include details that only locals would know.      Like the old church bell? It rings every Friday night, and no one knows why. Maybe Helen Moss is connected to that too?      I like that! We can weave in the bell as a symbol of her presence. It adds a haunting element to the story. I’m planning to include a scene where the bell rings out of nowhere, and Helen appears.

Okay, I’m just trying to figure out what’s in this packet of spices. Is it supposed to be for the lentil curry or the bolognese?      Oh, that’s the shmeat mix we got from the store. I thought it would be a good way to experiment without having to buy a whole chicken. It’s supposed to mimic real meat, right?      Yeah, but I still can’t get over the idea of eating something that’s not actually from an animal. Even if it’s cultured, it feels like we’re just pretending we’re not supporting animal cruelty.      I mean, I get it, but the environmental impact of meat farming is just too big. I’ve been reading up on it—it’s not just about the animals, it’s about the land, the water, the methane emissions. It’s all so overwhelming.      And then there are the ethical concerns. Like, how do you feel when you see a documentary about factory farming? I can’t even watch the whole thing. It’s too much. I mean, do we have a choice?      I think we do. I’ve been trying to tell people that even if we buy shmeat, we’re still part of a system that profits from animal exploitation. But maybe that’s just me being overly sensitive.      Maybe, but I don’t know. I’ve started taking vitamin tablets to make sure I’m getting enough B12, just in case. I’m also trying to switch to a more plant-based diet, but it’s not always easy.      I feel you. I’ve been experimenting with different recipes, and it’s actually been fun. I even tried making a bolognese with shmeat and it tasted surprisingly good. I think it’s easier to get used to it if you’re not thinking about the source.      I still can’t bring myself to eat meat, though. I’ve done some research on hunting versus factory farming, and honestly, I think the latter is just worse. There’s a kind of systematic oppression in how animals are treated.      Yeah, I’ve thought about that too. It’s like the whole system is built on the idea that animals are just resources. But maybe if more people start using shmeat or plant-based products, we can push for change.      I hope so. It’s all so complicated, though.

I just can’t believe how long it’s been since we threw that old washing machine out. I think it was over ten years ago, wasn’t it? Yeah, I remember that. I was only about eight or nine then, and I used to sit on the floor, watching the whole thing go down. It was like watching a horror movie in slow motion. I still get flashbacks of that day. And I still hear the sound of it every now and then in my head. But I suppose it was time. We’re better off with the new one now, even if it still smells a little like old socks sometimes. It feels more like a real celebration. But I think this year, we might try to do something similar. I’ve been thinking about it.

So, I've been meaning to ask you both about that butterfly fork you mentioned the other day. I saw it on a design blog—like, it's got these tiny wings on the tines, right? It’s a chance to pause and think about what we’ve lost and what we’ve gained. I think it’s a way to connect with history, even if it’s painful. Speaking of history, have you two heard about the Russia situation? It’s getting complicated.

So, I've been thinking about our holiday plans for next summer. I was just checking the website for Adventure Island and thought, maybe we could take the kids there? So, did you hear about the new school rules? I think they’re making us wear uniforms all year round now. No way, really? That’s brutal. Dude’s got a broken arm now. Oh no, that’s rough. I was going to ride my bike to the party tomorrow. Maybe I should take the bus instead. I don’t want to end up in the hospital. Yeah, maybe we should all take the bus. It’s safer, and we can grab some snacks on the way. I’m not sure if I’ll be able to go to the party, though. My parents are going out of town. That’s a bummer.

I just got a text from my cousin. She's going to be late getting back from her trip. She said she got stuck in some construction site traffic on the A1. It’s a win-win. Yeah, I’ll give it a shot. I’ve got a feeling it’ll be easier than dealing with the traffic. Besides, the weather is supposed to be nice this weekend. I could take a longer ride.

I can't believe we've been trying to order Chinese food for an hour now. The app keeps crashing, and the website is so slow. I’m about to give up and just cook something. I can choose the menu and then you can pick what you want.

I've been thinking a lot about the NHS lately. You know, how it's changing, and how it's affecting people's lives. I’ve been thinking about the state of the country lately, you know? The welfare system is under more pressure than ever. That’s a bit of a heavy topic, but fair enough. You know, I was in the same boat once. I was laid off back in the late '80s, and I never really found a job again. I mean, I’ve had my fair share of ups and downs, but I’m still here. I guess it’s about making the best of what you've got.

Oh, I just got an email from the university about the new corpus update. I’m so glad we’re finally getting the data sorted. I’ve been waiting for this for ages.      Yeah, I saw that too. I think it’s going to be a huge boost for our research. But honestly, I still can’t believe how much work goes into maintaining all these linguistic databases. It’s like a never-ending puzzle.      It definitely is. I mean, I’ve been helping out with the administrative side of things, and it’s not as simple as it looks. There are so many layers to it. I think Speaker_1’s role is the most hands-on though.      I wouldn’t say it’s hands-on. It’s more like organizing the chaos, if you know what I mean. But honestly, it’s pretty rewarding. I love being in the middle of all this language research.      Speaking of which, I was just talking to a colleague about how we should be collaborating more with the publishing side. They have access to so many resources that could really elevate our research. Have you guys thought about it?      Oh, I wouldn’t say we’re  exactly  the publishing side. I’m more on the editorial end. But I do work closely with the press, so maybe there's potential. Though I still think the biggest challenge is getting everyone on the same page.      That’s the real key here, isn’t it? No matter how much data we collect or how many projects we run, it all comes down to communication. We’re all part of a larger network, even if we don’t always see it.      Absolutely. And I think that’s why we’re all here, right? To learn, to grow, and to support each other. It’s not just about the work—we’re building something together.      That’s what makes this place special. Even though we come from different backgrounds, we all share this passion for language. It’s like the work we do becomes part of something bigger.      To language, to research, and to the crazy, wonderful people who make it all happen.      To Cambridge, to the press, and to the future of language studies.      And to the next big breakthrough.      And to not losing sight of the small things in all the chaos.      And to not burning out in the process.

So, do you remember that episode of  Doctor Who  where they went to a parallel universe and everything was like... but backwards? I swear, the whole thing was just a giant time loop. Oh, that one! Right, I’ve got everything we need for the week, but let me double-check. We’ve got the milk, eggs, and bread, but I think we might need more pasta. I think I just made a ton of noise. Anyway, I was going to ask—have you all seen the new SAT NAV device they’re selling? I got one, and it’s actually pretty good. I can't believe it's already December. You know, I’ve been feeling so down lately, like the light is just too bleak. I think it’s SAD. I’ve been struggling with sleep and just not feeling like doing anything. I know, I’ve felt the same. It’s so weird being so far from home. I miss the birds singing in the morning and the rain not being a gloomy thing—it just feels like the world has changed. It’s funny, isn’t it? I remember when I lived in Cambridge, the rain was always a peaceful sound. Now, in Tarnow, it just feels so heavy. Have you heard the football results yet? So, I just got a text from my sister saying her new boyfriend’s got a tattoo of a flamingo on his bicep. I don’t know what that’s about, but I’m guessing it’s a bad idea.      Flamingos? Yeah, I think that’s what dating is all about, right? Finding someone who gets you and likes your style. Not just the clothes, but the whole package.      I agree. I think it’s more about shared interests than looks, though. I mean, I’m not into fashion the way she is, but I can appreciate it. So, have you started dating anyone yet?      Not really. I just had the most bizarre experience today. I was walking through Gordon Square and this guy in a red hoodie started shouting at me in Chinese. I had no idea what he was saying, but he kept pointing at my bag. Then I realized he was trying to ask if I had a mobile phone. He was probably looking for someone to help him with WeChat. That sounds like a typical encounter in London. You’ve got all these Chinese guests walking around, and they’re so used to using WeChat, they think it’s the universal language. I remember once when I was teaching TEFL in China, I tried to use WeChat with my students, and they were all confused because the app was still called “WeChat” in English, but they called it something else in Mandarin. It was ridiculous. You're not wrong. I’ve been thinking a lot about teaching English in China lately. I’m actually considering taking on a PhD supervision role for someone wanting to go into TEFL. It’s such a competitive field, though, and the demand is so high. I mean, I’ve seen so many people trying to get into China, and not all of them are prepared for the cultural differences. Did you know that in some parts of China, they still have the death penalty? That’s pretty shocking. Yeah, I know. I actually read an article about how some of the more remote areas of China still enforce it for certain crimes. It’s not something you read about in the headlines, but it’s part of the landscape. I also heard a story about a colleague of mine who had a friend from Tibet. He said the landscape there is absolutely stunning, but the wildlife – like the pandas and bears – is quite different from what you see in the UK. I mean, the bears there are bigger than anything I’ve ever seen. That sounds amazing. I’ve always wanted to visit Tibet. My sister went there a few years ago and said the altitude was a killer. I’m not sure I’d be ready for that. Speaking of which, I saw a boy recently catching a pigeon in the park. He was so cute, just holding it like it was a pet. It reminded me of the time I lived in Devon and used to see these amazing birds flying over the cliffs.

So, do you know what’s going on with the car? I’ve been trying to get it started for like twenty minutes, and it just won’t budge. Yeah, I noticed. You think it’s the battery? Or maybe the starter? I mean, it’s been a bit of a nightmare ever since we drove it to the countryside last week. Yeah, I thought maybe it was the battery. I remember you saying you filled it up last weekend, but maybe there was some water in it or something. Or maybe it’s just the fuel pump. You’re right, I did say that. But I didn’t think it was a problem. I mean, I’ve driven it before and it worked fine. Hmmm… Maybe we should get it looked at by a mechanic, or at least bring it to the garage. I was just thinking the same thing. We can’t be stuck out here all day. We still have to get back to the city for the meeting tomorrow. Yeah, that’s true. I was hoping we could make it back in time. I know the meeting’s not that important, but it’s better to be safe than sorry. Exactly. And if we can’t get it fixed today, maybe we should rent a car from the airport. I’ve got a friend who works there, and he said they have a good deal on weekend rentals. That’s a good idea. I mean, we wouldn’t want to be stuck here all night. It’s not like we can just walk to the nearest town. Right, and we’re not even that far from the motorway. If we can get it running, maybe we can head to the nearest service station and see if they can help. I hope so. This is such a pain. I feel like we’re always dealing with car problems. I know, it’s part of owning a car, I guess. But man, I’d go for a rental next time if I had the chance. I’ll admit, I’m a bit tired of it. But I guess we’ll deal with it. Let’s just make sure we don’t end up stranded.

So, I’ve been feeling really off lately. Not sure if it’s just stress from work or something more serious. I’ve been getting these headaches and feeling really tired, even after a full night’s sleep. That sounds rough. You should probably see a doctor, yeah? I mean, I know you’re busy with events and everything, but your health comes first. You can’t keep pushing yourself like this. I know, but with the upcoming conference next week, I can’t just take a break. I’m already behind on a few things, and I don’t want to let the team down. It’s not like we’re all stuck in the same situation. Exactly. I think it’s important to take a step back sometimes and just enjoy the little things. Like, I’m actually looking forward to some quiet time with my family this weekend. It’s been a while since I’ve had a proper break. That sounds nice.

I can't believe I just got a call from Sarah saying she's moving to Manchester. I mean, we've worked together for nearly two years, and now she's gone. I feel like I've lost a friend. I know, it's so weird. I remember when she first started at the hospital, she was so nervous. But she grew into such a great nurse. I guess it's just a part of life, though. Everyone moves on. You're one of the people who makes things run smoothly. I've been meaning to talk to you about something—about the new project at work. I think you'd be a great fit for it. Really? I’d love that.
